STUDYQURAN:6:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:intro/r9.speaker: Some early authorities
STUDYQURAN:6:intro/r9.claim: Some early authorities considered certain verses, possibly those listed, to have been revealed in Madinah.
STUDYQURAN:6:intro/r9.anchor: Some early authorities, however, considered certain verses, perhaps vv. 20, 23, 91, 93, 114, 141, and 151–53, to have been revealed in Madinah

BURSEVI:v3p90/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p90/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p90/r3.claim: These three verses contain ten comprehensive duties, unchanged across revealed books, peoples, and eras; whoever practices them enters Paradise, while whoever abandons them enters Hell.
BURSEVI:v3p90/r3.anchor: هذه الآيات الثلاث إلى قوله : {لعلكم تتقون} تشتمل على عشر خصال جامعة للخير كله لم ينسخهن شيء

BURSEVI:v3p91/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p91/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p91/r3.claim: Do not approach an orphan’s property in any way; an orphan is a human without a father or an animal without a mother, and the address is to guardians and trustees.
BURSEVI:v3p91/r3.anchor: {ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم} أي : لا تتعرضوا له بوجه من الوجوه واليتيم من الإنسان من لا أب له

BURSEVI:v3p91#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p91#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p91#2/r1.claim: The sole exception is the best way of handling the orphan’s estate, such as preserving and investing it.
BURSEVI:v3p91#2/r1.anchor: {إلا بالتى هى أحسن} إلا بالخصلة التي هي أحسن ما يفعل بماله كحفظه وتثميره.

BURSEVI:v3p91#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p91#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p91#2/r2.claim: The endpoint applies to the implied duty to safeguard the estate: keep it until the orphan reaches maturity and sound judgment, then deliver it.
BURSEVI:v3p91#2/r2.anchor: {حتى يبلغ أشده} غاية لما يفهم من الاستثناء لا للنهي كأنه قيل احفظوه

BURSEVI:v3p91#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p91#2/r3.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BURSEVI:v3p91#2/r3.claim: Abu Hanifa sets the age of maturity at twenty-five, unless the person is mentally deficient.
BURSEVI:v3p91#2/r3.anchor: وجعل أبو حنيفة غاية الأشد خمسا وعشرين سنة فإذا بلغها دفع إليه ماله

BURSEVI:v3p91#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p91#2/r4.speaker: الجوهري
BURSEVI:v3p91#2/r4.claim: Al-Jawhari glosses ashudd as strength, spanning ages eighteen to thirty; it is an unusual singular pattern, while Sibawayh calls its singular shiddah.
BURSEVI:v3p91#2/r4.anchor: قال الجوهري : {حتى يبلغ أشده} أي : قوته وهو ما بين ثماني عشرة إلى ثلاثين

BURSEVI:v3p91#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p91#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p91#2/r5.claim: This sixth duty protects an orphan’s property because of the orphan’s vulnerability and God’s command to care for it.
BURSEVI:v3p91#2/r5.anchor: وهذا هو الحكم السادس ، وإنما وصى الله تعالى بحفظ مال اليتيم لأنه عاجز

BURSEVI:v3p91#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p91#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p91#2/r6.claim: A Persian couplet says even the mighty throne trembles when an orphan’s heart weeps.
BURSEVI:v3p91#2/r6.anchor:
ألا تانكريدكه عرش عظيم
بلرزد همي ون بكريديتيم

BURSEVI:v3p91#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p91#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p91#3/r1.claim: Fulfill measures for measured goods and scales for weighed goods justly; qist describes the state of fair fulfillment.
BURSEVI:v3p91#3/r1.anchor: {وأوفوا الكيل} في المكيلات أي أتموه ولا تنقصوا منه شيئا {والميزان} في الموزونات

BURSEVI:v3p91#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p91#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p91#3/r2.claim: The apparent repetition of justice clarifies both sides: the seller must give the full due, and the buyer must accept it without demanding extra.
BURSEVI:v3p91#3/r2.anchor: أمر المعطي بإيفاء ذي الحق حقه من غير نقصان وأمر صاحب الحق بأخذه من غير طلب زيادة

BURSEVI:v3p91#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p91#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p91#3/r3.claim: Because justice in measurement is difficult, people must do their best; small unintended discrepancies from diligent weighing are forgiven, while deliberate shortchanging is not.
BURSEVI:v3p91#3/r3.anchor: وذكره عقيب الأمر للإيذان بأن مراعاة العدل عسير فعليكم بما في وسعكم

BURSEVI:v3p91#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p91#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p91#3/r4.claim: One dying trader could not utter the testimony of faith because, he said, the tongue of the scales lay on his tongue, despite his claim to give full weight.
BURSEVI:v3p91#3/r4.anchor: يعامل الناس بالميزان ، قل : لا إله إلا الله فقال : ما أقدر أقولها ، لسان الميزان على لساني

BURSEVI:v3p91#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p91#3/r5.speaker: مالك بن دينار
BURSEVI:v3p91#3/r5.claim: Malik ibn Dinar visited a dying neighbor who said two mountains of fire stood before him; his family said he used separate measures for buying and selling, and breaking them did not ease his agony.
BURSEVI:v3p91#3/r5.anchor: وعن مالك بن دينار أنه دخل على جار له احتضر فقال يا مالك جبلان من النار بين يدي

BURSEVI:v3p91#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p91#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p91#3/r6.claim: This is the seventh duty. Inwardly, fulfill the measure of one’s lifetime and the scale of divine rights, and pursue spiritual effort and moderation according to capacity.
BURSEVI:v3p91#3/r6.anchor:
وهذا هو الحكم السابع.
والإشارة أوفوا بكيل العمر ، وميزان الشرع حقوق الربوبية

BURSEVI:v3p91#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p91#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p91#3/r7.claim: The Persian verse says each person proceeds according to the measure of their own wings and strength.
BURSEVI:v3p91#3/r7.anchor: لا نكلف نفسا في إيفاء الحقوق واستيفاء الحظوظ إلا بحسب استعدادها

BURSEVI:v3p91#4/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p91#4/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p91#4/r1.claim: In judgment, testimony, and speech, be just even toward relatives; truth and God’s pleasure must override kinship.
BURSEVI:v3p91#4/r1.anchor:
{وإذا قلتم} قولا في حكومة أو شهادة أو نحوهما.
{فاعدلوا} فيه {ولو كان}

BURSEVI:v3p91#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p91#4/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p91#4/r2.claim: This eighth duty’s inward truth is to speak of and through God; only people of realization can do so without self-interest and claims.
BURSEVI:v3p91#4/r2.anchor: وحقيقة العدل في الكلام أن يذكر الله ، ولا يذكر معه غيره وأن يتكلموفي الله وبالله

BURSEVI:v3p91#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p91#4/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p91#4/r3.claim: The Persian verse invokes the hoopoe as a model for learning truthful communication and its message.
BURSEVI:v3p91#4/r3.anchor:
بأنك هدهدكر بياموزد فتى
راز هدهكوو يغام سبا

BURSEVI:v3p91#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p91#4/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p91#4/r4.claim: Fulfill every covenant commanded by God, including justice and religious duties, vows to God, or agreements between people, which God requires be kept.
BURSEVI:v3p91#4/r4.anchor: {وبعهد الله أوفوا} أي : ما عهد إليكم أي عهد كان من ملازمة العدل وتأدية أحكام الشرع

BURSEVI:v3p91#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p91#4/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p91#4/r5.claim: This is the ninth duty; inwardly, covenant means worshipping and loving only one’s Lord and seeing none besides Him.
BURSEVI:v3p91#4/r5.anchor: وهذا هو الحكم التاسع ، وحقيقة العهد أن لا يعبد إلا مولاه ولا يحب إلا إياه

BURSEVI:v3p91#4/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p91#4/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p91#4/r6.claim: The Persian verses describe love for the Friend as one covenant extending from primordial morning to the end of time.
BURSEVI:v3p91#4/r6.anchor:
ازدم صبح ازل تا آخر شام ابد
دوستى ومهر بريك عهد ويك ميثاق بود

BURSEVI:v3p92/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p92/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p92/r1.claim: The reminder refers to the four duties just detailed and commands people to remember and act on them.
BURSEVI:v3p92/r1.anchor:
{ذالكم} إشارة إلى ما فصل من التكاليف الأربعة.
{وصاكم به} أمركم به أمرا مؤكدا

QASHANI:6:152-153/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:152-153/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:152-153/r1.claim: The three vice classes together entail injustice, the greatest vice; corresponding virtues entail justice, which includes them all.
QASHANI:6:152-153/r1.anchor: أن الرذائل الثلاث مستلزمة باجتماعها رذيلة الجور التي هي أعظمها وجماعها

QASHANI:6:152-153/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:152-153/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:152-153/r2.claim: Protect the orphan's property, using it only for preservation and investment until maturity, not for one's needs or waste.
QASHANI:6:152-153/r2.anchor: إلا بالخصلة التي هي أحسن من حفظه وتثميره

QASHANI:6:152-153/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:152-153/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:152-153/r3.claim: After detailing four vices, the passage summarizes four virtues because their opposites are clear; all virtues are included in justice.
QASHANI:6:152-153/r3.anchor: ولما بين تحريم أجناس الرذائل الأربع بأسرها على التفصيل أمر بإيجاب الفضائل الأربع بالإجمال، إذ تفصيل الرذائل يغني عن تفصيل مقابلاتها

QASHANI:6:152-153/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:152-153/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:152-153/r4.claim: Fair measure and weight mean maintaining justice in all dealings; just speech means truth, including when speaking for or against a relative.
QASHANI:6:152-153/r4.anchor: أي: حافظوا على العدل فيما بينكم وبين الخلق مطلقا

QASHANI:6:152-153/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:152-153/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:152-153/r5.claim: Fulfilling God's covenant means unity, obedience, and all obligations arising from the primordial covenant renewed by a later pledge.
QASHANI:6:152-153/r5.anchor: أي: بالتوحيد والطاعة وكل ما بينكم وبين الله من لوازم العهد السابق بالعقد اللاحق

QASHANI:6:152-153/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:152-153/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:152-153/r6.claim: The path of virtue and unity is difficult, especially the balanced middle in action; Qashani says these instructions encompass all vices and virtues.
QASHANI:6:152-153/r6.anchor: ولما كان سلوك طريقة الفضيلة التي هي طريقة الوحدة والتوجه إلى الحق صعبا، كما قيل: أدق من الشعرة وأحد من السيف

QASHANI:6:152-153/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:152-153/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QASHANI:6:152-153/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas calls these decisive verses that no scripture has abrogated; Qashani reports agreement among the scriptural communities and religious schools.
QASHANI:6:152-153/r7.anchor: ولهذا قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنه: إن هذه آيات محكمات لم ينسخهن شيء من جميع الكتب.

QASHANI:6:152-153/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:152-153/r8.speaker: كعب الأحبار
QASHANI:6:152-153/r8.claim: Ka'b al-Ahbar swears that these were the first words in the Torah.
QASHANI:6:152-153/r8.anchor: وقال كعب الأحبار: والذي نفس كعب بيده إنها لأول شيء في التوراة.

SULAMI:v1p216#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p216#4/r1.speaker: أبو سليمان
SULAMI:v1p216#4/r1.claim: When speaking, learn through remembrance of God.
SULAMI:v1p216#4/r1.anchor: قال أبو سليمان في هذه الآية : إذا تكلمتم فتعلموا بذكره

SULAMI:v1p216#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p216#4/r2.speaker: محمد بن حامد العدل
SULAMI:v1p216#4/r2.claim: Speech should concern matters that bring no immediate or eventual liability on the speaker.
SULAMI:v1p216#4/r2.anchor: وقال محمد بن حامد العدل : في الكلام ما لا يكون على صاحبه في ذلك تبعة عاجلا وآجلا

SULAMI:v1p216#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p216#4/r3.speaker: الجوزجاني
SULAMI:v1p216#4/r3.claim: The most important covenant is enjoining right and forbidding wrong, beginning with disciplining oneself before correcting others.
SULAMI:v1p216#4/r3.anchor: قال الجوزجاني : العهود كثيرة وأحق العهود بالوفاء الامر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر فأمر نفسك بالمعروف

SULAMI:v1p216#4/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p216#4/r4.speaker: الجوزجاني
SULAMI:v1p216#4/r4.claim: If the self resists goodness or leaving wrong, train it through hunger, night vigil, remembrance, righteous company, travel, solitude, limited speech, and patience before guiding others.
SULAMI:v1p216#4/r4.anchor: فإن قبلت منك وإلا روضها بالجوع والسهر وكثرة الذكر ومجالسة الصالحين

TUSTARI:6:152/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:6:152/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:6:152/r1.claim: Truthful speech is speech about God, through God, for God, or with God; others speak about and for themselves, or speak of people while forgetting themselves and going astray.
TUSTARI:6:152/r1.anchor: قال: تكلم أهل الصدق على أربعة أوجه، قوم تكلموا في الله وبالله ولله ومع الله

TUSTARI:6:152/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:6:152/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:6:152/r2.claim: Leave speech to knowledge and speak only when necessary, avoiding words that risk sin.
TUSTARI:6:152/r2.anchor: فاتركوا الكلام للعلم، ثم تكلموا على الضرورة تسلموا من آفات الكلام.

TUSTARI:6:152/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:6:152/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:6:152/r3.claim: Assuming evil removes certainty, irrelevant speech removes truthfulness, and using the limbs for other than God removes scrupulousness; losing all three ruins a person.
TUSTARI:6:152/r3.anchor: ثم قال: من ظن [ظن السوء] حرم اليقين، ومن تكلم بما لا يعنيه حرم الصدق

TUSTARI:6:152/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:6:152/r4.speaker: الربيع بن خثيم
TUSTARI:6:152/r4.claim: Since he is not satisfied with himself, he will not devote himself to criticizing others; fear God regarding others' sins and focus urgently on your own.
TUSTARI:6:152/r4.anchor: ما أنا عن نفسي براض فأتفرغ من ذم نفسي

NAHHAS:v2p106/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p106/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p106/r6.claim: The whole passage is prohibitive, so the nūn is dropped; fulfill God’s covenant when making a covenant with God or swearing to a person.
NAHHAS:v2p106/r6.anchor: نهي كله فلذلك حذفت منه النون ( وبعهد الله أوفوا ) أي إذا عاهدتم الله جل وعز على شيء

NAHHAS:v2p106/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p106/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p106/r7.claim: In ذلكم وصاكم به, tāʾ assimilates to dhāl because they are close; it may also be omitted where its meaning remains clear.
NAHHAS:v2p106/r7.anchor: مثل الأول وأدغمت التاء في الذال لقربها منها ويجوز حذفها للدلالة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418#2/r1.claim: After the prohibition, people separated orphan property until food spoiled; God then permitted mixing with orphans as brothers (2:220), distinguishing reformers from corrupters.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : لما نزلت : ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم الا بالتي هي احسن عزلوا اموال اليتامي ، حتى جعل الطعام يفسد واللحم ينتن

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418#2/r2.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418#2/r2.claim: A guardian should not use the orphan's property even for a cap or turban.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418#2/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة ، في قوله : ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم الا بالتي هي احسن قال : ليس لولي اليتيم ان يلبس قلنسوة ولا عمامة من ماله ، ولكن يده مع يده .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418#2/r3.speaker: عطية
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418#2/r3.claim: The best use includes investing the orphan's money in trade for profit.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418#2/r3.anchor: عن عطية : ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم الا بالتي هي احسن ، قال : طلب التجارة فيه والربح فيه .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418#2/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418#2/r4.claim: One view says the guardian may not buy anything from the orphan's estate.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي اسحاق ، في قوله : ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم الا بالتي هي احسن قال : لا يشتري منه شيئا

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418#2/r5.speaker: الضحاك، السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418#2/r5.claim: The guardian should seek benefit for the orphan in his property.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418#2/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك : ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم الا بالتي هي احسن ، قال : يبتغي اليتيم في ماله . وروى عن السدي نحو ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418#2/r6.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418#2/r6.claim: Best use allows a poor guardian reasonable food but requires a wealthy one to abstain; the verse mentions eating, not clothing, as in 4:6.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418#2/r6.anchor: عبد الرحمن ابن زيد بن اسلم في قوله : ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم الا بالتي هي احسن

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418#2/r7.speaker: حسن بن صالح
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418#2/r7.claim: The guardian should seek God's bounty for the orphan and take nothing himself.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1418#2/r7.anchor: حسن بن صالح في هذه الاية : ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم الا بالتي هي احسن قال : يبتغي له من فضل الله

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r1.claim: One definition of reaching maturity is age thirty-three.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد عن ابن عباس : اشده ، قال : ثلاث وثلاثون . وروى عن مجاهد وقتادة نحو ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r2.claim: An alternative sets maturity at forty.

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r3.speaker: الشعبي، ربيعة، زيد بن أسلم، مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r3.claim: Another view defines maturity as puberty, when good and bad deeds begin to be recorded.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r3.anchor: عن الشعبي انه قال الاشدك الحلم اذا كتبت له الحسنات وكتبت عليه السيئات . وروى عن ربيعة وزيد بن اسلم ومالك ، قالوا : الحلم .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r4.claim: One report sets maturity at eighteen.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير : قوله : حتى يبلغ اشده ، قال : ثماني عشرة سنة .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r5.claim: An alternative sets maturity at thirty.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r5.anchor: عن السدي : قوله : حتى يبلغ اشده ، اما اشده فثلاثون سنة .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r6.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r6.claim: Another report sets maturity at twenty-five.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r6.anchor: عن عكرمة ، في قوله : اشده ، قال : خمس وعشرون سنة .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r7.speaker: محمد بن قيس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r7.claim: Another report sets maturity at fifteen.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r7.anchor: عن محمد بن قيس : قوله : اشده خمس عشرة سنة .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r8.claim: Fair measure and weight mean justice.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، في قول الله : بالقسط ، قال : يعني بالعدل .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r9.claim: God made religious obligations manageable for believers, as also stated in 22:78.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، في قوله : لا نكلف نفسا الا وسعها قال : هم المؤمنون ، وسع الله عليهم امر دينهم فقال : ما جعل عليكم في الدين من حرج .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r10.claim: A person's capacity means his ability.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1419/r10.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : الا وسعها يعني : الا طاقتها .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1420/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1420/r1.speaker: الشعبي
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1420/r1.claim: Capacity means only what a person has done for himself.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1420/r1.anchor: عن عامر الشعبي : لا نكلف نفسا الا وسعها : الا ما عملت لها .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1420/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1420/r2.speaker: سفيان
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1420/r2.claim: Capacity here means performing the obligations.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1420/r2.anchor: عن سفيان ، في قوله : لا نكلف نفسا الا وسعها قال : اداء الفرائض .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1420/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1420/r3.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1420/r3.claim: To speak justly means to tell the truth.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1420/r3.anchor: قال : سمعت عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن اسلم ، في قوله : واذا قلتم فاعدلوا ، قال : قولوا الحق .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1420/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1420/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1420/r4.claim: Tell the truth even when speaking about a relative.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1420/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير : قوله : واذا قلتم فاعدلوا ولو كان ذا قربى ، يعني : ولو كان قرابتك فقل فيه الحق .

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1420/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1420/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1420/r5.claim: Fulfilling God's covenant includes keeping confirmed vows, as also stated in 16:91.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1420/r5.anchor: وبه عن سعيد بن جبير في قول الله تعالى : وبعهد الله اوفوا وقوله في النحل : واوفوا بعهد الله اذا عاهدتم ، وقوله : ولا تنقضوا الايمان بعد توكيدها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p156/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p156/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p156/r1.claim: The three linked groups are social order opened by avoiding shirk, interpersonal and economic order opened by protecting orphan property, and the comprehensive principle of following Islam's straight path and avoiding deviant paths.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p156/r1.anchor: إلى ثلاثة أقسام : الأول : أحكام بها إصلاح الحالة الاجتماعية العامة بين الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p156/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p156/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p156/r2.claim: Each of the three sections is closed with a testament from God, repeated three times.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p156/r2.anchor: وقد ذيل كل قسم من هذه الأقسام بالوصاية به بقوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p162#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p162#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p162#2/r1.claim: This group of prohibitions protects human dealings, builds the Muslim community and its civic order, and establishes mutual trust; it begins with the vulnerable orphan who cannot defend property rights.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p162#2/r1.anchor: عطف محرمات ترجع إلى حفظ قواع التعامل بين الناس لإقامة قواعد الجامعة الإسلامية ومدنيتها وتحقيق ثقة الناس بعضهم ببعض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p162#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p162#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p162#2/r2.claim: Approaching an orphan's property means dealing with it; the exception allows only the best beneficial course, with an omitted feminine noun such as state or act understood after the relative pronoun.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p162#2/r2.anchor: والقربان كناية عن ملابسة مال اليتيم . والتصرف فيه كما تقدم آنفا في قوله : { ولا تقربوا الفواحش

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p162#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p162#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p162#2/r3.claim: The feminine relative can stand for an omitted state or act, as in the command to repel evil in the best manner and the fixed proverb after the lesser and greater calamity; Salmi's line illustrates the proverb.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p162#2/r3.anchor: ومنه قوله تعالى : { ادفع بالتي هي أحسن السيئة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p162#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p162#2/r4.speaker: سلمي بن ربيعة الضبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p162#2/r4.claim: His verse uses the idiom اللتيا والتي for the lesser and greater calamities, illustrating the conventional feminine-relative construction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p162#2/r4.anchor:
كما قال سلمي بن ربيعة الضبي :
ولقد رأبت ثأى العشيرة بينها
وكفيت جانبها اللتيا والتي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p162#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p162#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p162#2/r5.claim: Ahsan means beneficial, not harmful to the orphan or the property; the command says do not approach, warning against even the slightest taking because the orphan cannot defend himself.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p162#2/r5.anchor: اسم تفضيل مسلوب المفاضلة ، أي الحسنة ، وهي النافعة التي لا ضر فيها لليتيم ولا لماله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p164/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p164/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p164/r1.claim: The order concerns trade: dates and raisins were sold by measure and gold and silver by weight, while traders shorted buyers to increase profit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p164/r1.anchor: وذلك في التبايع ، فقد كانوا يبيعون التمر والزبيب كيلا ، وكانوا يتوازنون الذهب والفضة ، فكانوا يطففون حرصا على الربح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p164/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p164/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p164/r2.claim: The positive command to fulfill, unlike Shuayb's prohibition on reducing measures, focuses attention on doing justice and recalls Arabs' boast of generosity, exposing their moral inconsistency.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p164/r2.anchor: وعدل عن أن يأتي فيه بالنهي عن التطفيف كما في قول شعيب : { ولا تنقصوا المكيال والميزان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p164/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p164/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p164/r3.claim: The preposition with fairness means to act justly and not deprive a customer of the amount due.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p164/r3.anchor: أي أوفوا متلبسين بالعدل بأن لا تظلموا المكتال حقه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p164/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p164/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p164/r4.claim: The capacity clause qualifies exact measurement: people owe what they reasonably judge fair, not perfect accuracy to the smallest grain, so fear of error will not halt useful trade.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p164/r4.anchor: لا نكلفكم تمام القسط في الكيل والميزان بالحبة والذرة ولكنا نكلفكم ما تظنون أنه عدل ووفاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p164/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p164/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p164/r5.claim: The shift to God's direct first-person voice makes this qualification a special favor and confirms the messenger; fair measure protects buyers who are distracted while the seller controls the measure, so stronger forms of taking property are even more forbidden.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p164/r5.anchor: فتولى الله خطاب الناس فيه بطريق التكلم مباشرة زيادة في المنة ، وتصديقا للمبلغ ، فالوصاية بإيفاء الكيل والميزان راجعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p166/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p166/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p166/r1.claim: The capacity clause may qualify fair measures as requiring reasonable effort, or may summarize that all preceding duties lie within people's ability; the latter reading generalizes the point made at 2:286.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p166/r1.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون جملة : { لا نكلف نفسا إلا وسعها } تذييلا للجمل التي قبلها ، تسجيلا عليهم بأن جميع ما دعوا إليه هو في طاقتهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p166/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p166/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p166/r2.claim: The command to speak justly covers all speech-mediated dealings: testimony, judgment, evaluations, advice, reconciliation, descriptions, promises, wills, oaths, praise, and insults or slander.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p166/r2.anchor: هذا جامع كل المعاملات بين الناس بواسطة الكلام وهي الشهادة ، والقضاء ، والتعديل ، والتجريح ، والمشاورة ، والصلح بين الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p166/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p166/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p166/r3.claim: Justice in speech means not violating rights: disclose defects, avoid invented defects or false prices, give honest evaluations and advice, speak truth in reconciliation and testimony, honor promises and inheritance rights, avoid false oaths, praise truthfully, and refrain from insults even if deserved.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p166/r3.anchor: والعدل في ذلك أن لا يكون في القول شيء من الاعتداء على الحقوق : بإبطالها ، أو إخفائها ، مثل كتمان عيوب المبيع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p166/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p166/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p166/r4.claim: The conditional wording leaves room for silence when one cannot speak justly, but no license to speak unjustly; some silence is itself obligatory.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p166/r4.anchor: وفي التعليق بأداة الشرط في قوله : { وإذا قلتم } إشارة إلى أن المرء في سعة من السكوت إن خشي قول العدل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p166/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p166/r5.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p166/r5.claim: A report in the Muwatta says Umar struck or nearly struck a man who told a suitor that the man's sister had previously transgressed, then asked why he had shared the information.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p166/r5.anchor: وفي ( الموطأ ) أن رجلا خطب إلى رجل أخته فذكر الأخ أنها قد كانت أحدثت فبلغ ذلك عمر بن الخطاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p167/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p167/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p167/r1.claim: The waw is circumstantial and law concessive, emphasizing even the exceptional case of kinship; the implied person discussed may be related to the speaker, whose bias must not displace justice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p167/r1.anchor: والواو في قوله : { ولو كان } واو الحال ، ولو وصلية تفيد المبالغة في الحال التي من شأنها أن يظن السامع عدم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p167/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p167/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p167/r2.claim: Whether speaking for or against a relative, one must not conceal a liability, invent a right, or absolve wrongdoing; the parallel rule for witness and judge appears at 4:135.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p167/r2.anchor: إذا قلتم قولا لأجله أو عليه فاعدلوا ولا تقولوا غير الحق ، لا لدفع ضره بأن تغمصوا الحق الذي عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p167/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p167/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p167/r3.claim: Positive command to make speech just better serves disclosure of truth than merely forbidding falsehood; it also avoids condemning indirect speech allowed under fear, accommodation, or circumstances where no right is at stake.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p167/r3.anchor: وقد جاء طلب الحق في القول بصيغة الأمر بالعدل ، دون النهي عن الظلم أو الباطل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p167/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p167/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p167/r4.claim: A hadith says indirect expressions provide room to avoid lying, supporting the author's distinction between falsehood and permissible equivocal speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p167/r4.anchor: وتلك هي المعاريض التي ورد فيها حديث : ( إن في المعاريض لمندوحة عن الكذب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p167/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p167/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p167/r5.claim: God's covenant may mean rules God imposed, a pledge people made to God, or any human covenant God commands them to keep; the genitive preserves all these senses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p167/r5.anchor: أن تكون إضافة المصدر إلى الفاعل ، أي ما عهد الله به إليكم من الشرائع ، ويصح أن تكون إضافة المصدر إلى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p167/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p167/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p167/r6.claim: Because the address is to polytheists, the covenant includes their known alliances and peace agreements; calling it God's covenant reflects their practice of swearing oaths when contracting.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p167/r6.anchor: للمشركين تعين أن يكون العهد شيئا قد تقررت معرفته بينهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p169/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p169/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p169/r1.claim: The author cites الحارث بن حلزة’s verse as an example of Arabs praising fidelity to covenants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p169/r1.anchor:
واذكروا حلف ذي المجاز وما
قدم فيه العهود والكفلاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p169/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p169/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p169/r2.claim: The author cites عمرو بن كلثوم’s verse as an example of Arabs praising fidelity to covenants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p169/r2.anchor:
وقال عمرو بن كلثوم :
ونوجد نحن أمنعهم ذمارا
وأوفاهم إذا عقدوا يمينا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p169/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p169/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p169/r3.claim: Arab pacts against injustice in Mecca, including the Hilf al-Fudul and the Mutayyibin alliance, implemented God's promise to Abraham that Mecca be safe; persecuting vulnerable Muslims violated that safety and their own covenants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p169/r3.anchor: ومن العهود المقررة بينهم : حلف الفضول ، وحلف المطيبين ، وكلاهما كان في الجاهلية على نفي الظلم والجور عن القاطنين بمكة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p169/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p169/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p169/r4.claim: The covenant phrase is fronted to emphasize that fidelity to God's covenant matters most: if they prize keeping agreements, they should keep the covenant they chose, as in the contrast at 2:217.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p169/r4.anchor: وتقديم المجرور على عامله للاهتمام بأمر العهد وصرف ذهن السامع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170/r1.claim: The repeated closing formula ends this class of rules; remembrance is apt because the four duties were recognized Arab virtues, but desire and idolatry had made them forget.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170/r1.anchor: وجاء مع هذه الوصية بقوله : { لعلكم تذكرون } لأن هذه المطالب الأربعة عرف بين العرب أنها محامد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170/r2.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر وأبو جعفر ويعقوب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170/r2.claim: They read tadhakkarun with doubled dhāl, assimilating the second tāʾ into the dhāl after changing it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170/r2.anchor: نافع ، وابن كثير ، وأبو عمرو ، وابن عامر ، وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر ، وأبو جعفر ، ويعقوب : تذكرون بتشديد الذال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170/r3.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وعاصم في رواية حفص وخلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170/r3.claim: They read tadhakkarun with a light dhāl, deleting the second tāʾ for ease of pronunciation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p170/r3.anchor: وقرأ حمزة ، والكسائي ، وعاصم في رواية حفص ، وخلف بتخفيف الذال على حذف التاء الثانية تخفيفا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362#3/r1.claim: The ban on approaching orphan wealth covers every kind of management and blocks harmful means; the exception is what best preserves and grows it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362#3/r1.anchor: هذا نهي عن القرب الذي يعم وجوه التصرف، وفيه سد الذريعة، ثم استثنى ما يحسن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362#3/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362#3/r2.claim: Mujahid says the best management is trade for an orphan whose guardian has other means of support.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362#3/r2.anchor:
قال مجاهد: بالتي هي أحسن
التجارة فيه ممن كان من الناظرين له مال يعيش به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362#3/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362#3/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says a guardian without independent means may fairly support himself from the profits of managing the estate, since otherwise necessity may leave it unattended.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362#3/r3.anchor: فالأحسن أن ينظر ويأكل بالمعروف، قاله ابن زيد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362#3/r4.claim: Ashudd here means sound judgment, firmness in decisions, and good financial management.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362#3/r4.anchor: و «الأشد» جمع شد وجمع شدة، وهو هنا الحزم والنظر في الأمور وحسن التصرف فيها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362#3/r5.claim: Ashudd here is not the age forty mentioned elsewhere: these capacities can arise in youth, whereas that passage concerns experience and seasoned reason; commentators have conflated them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362#3/r5.anchor: وليس هذا بالأشد المقرون ببلوغ الأربعين، بل هذا يكون مع صغر السن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362#3/r6.speaker: ربيعة والشعبي ومالك وأبو حنيفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362#3/r6.claim: They define reaching maturity as puberty provided the person is not shown to be foolish; al-Suddi gives thirty years, another group thirty-three, and a group eighteen.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p362#3/r6.anchor: وقال ربيعة والشعبي ومالك فيما روي عنه وأبو حنيفة، «بلوغ الأشد» البلوغ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363/r1.speaker: الزجاج والنقاش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj weakens the eighteen-year view and prefers puberty with sound judgment; al-Naqqash reports a range from fifteen to thirty.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363/r1.anchor: وحكى الزجاج عن فرقة ثمانية عشرة سنة، وضعفه ورجح البلوغ مع الرشد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363/r2.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363/r2.claim: The author endorses the soundest and contextually apt view: puberty together with maturity and removal of foolishness, attributed to Malik.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363/r2.anchor: وهذا أصح الأقوال وأليقها بهذا الموضع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363/r3.claim: The commands to give full measure and weight require fairness in taking and giving; qisṭ means justice.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363/r3.anchor:
وأوفوا الكيل والميزان
الآية أمر بالاعتدال في الأخذ والإعطاء، و «القسط» العدل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363/r4.claim: No soul is charged beyond capacity: people must take feasible precautions, not achieve absolute exactness; al-Tabari says this relieves both buyer and seller from burdensome efforts to equalize every measure.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363/r4.anchor: يقتضي أن هذه الأوامر إنما هي فيما يقع تحت قدرة البشر من التحفظ والتحرز

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363/r5.claim: The command to speak justly includes testimony, rulings, and mediation, even when justice goes against one’s relatives.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363/r5.anchor:
وإذا قلتم فاعدلوا
يتضمن الشهادات والأحكام والتوسط بين الناس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363/r6.claim: God’s covenant may mean all obligations He imposed, or those obligations together with human agreements, whose preservation He commanded.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363/r6.anchor:
وبعهد الله
يحتمل أن يراد جميع ما عهده الله إلى عباده، ويحتمل أن يراد به جميع ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363/r7.claim: Laʿallakum is hope from the human perspective; reciters differ over light or doubled forms of tadhakkarūn and related verbs, with further specific variants noted for 19:67 and 25:62.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p363/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو «تذكرون» بتشديد الذال والكاف جميعا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r1.claim: An orphan’s property is singled out because weak oversight and the owner’s vulnerability make it especially tempting to seize.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r1.anchor: إنما خص مال اليتيم لأن الطمع فيه لقلة مراعيه وضعف مالكه أقوى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r2.claim: One interpretation permits a guardian to consume customary amounts while in need, according to Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn Zayd.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r2.anchor: أنه أكل الوصي المصلح للمال بالمعروف وقت حاجته قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi interpret the best manner as trading with the orphan’s property.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r3.anchor: التجارة فيه قاله سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد والضحاك والسدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r4.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r4.claim: Ibn al-Saʾib says it means preserving the property until it is delivered to the orphan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r4.anchor: أنه حفظه له إلى وقت تسليمه إليه قاله ابن السائب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj says to preserve and grow the property; “until maturity” implies keeping it safe until then and handing it over afterward.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r5.anchor: أنه حفظه عليه وتثميره له قاله الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r6.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r6.claim: Ibn Qutayba defines ashudd as the full strength of youth before decline; the term has several proposed singular forms, or no singular at all.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r6.anchor: فأما الأشد فهو استحكام قوة الشباب والسن قال ابن قتيبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r7.speaker: ابن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r7.claim: Ibn Jubayr transmits from Ibn ʿAbbas that ashudd is thirty-three years.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r7.anchor: أنه ثلاث وثلاثون سنة رواه ابن جبير عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r8.speaker: أبو صالح
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r8.claim: Abu Salih transmits from Ibn ʿAbbas that ashudd is between eighteen and thirty years.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r8.anchor: ما بين ثماني عشرة إلى ثلاثين سنة قاله أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r9.speaker: عائشة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r9.claim: A report from ʿAʾisha identifies ashudd as forty years.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r9.anchor: أربعون سنة روي عن عائشة عليها السلام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r10.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr and Muqatil say ashudd is eighteen years.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r10.anchor: ثماني عشرة سنة قاله سعيد بن جبير ومقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r11.speaker: عكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r11.claim: ʿIkrima gives twenty-five years as the age of ashudd.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r12.speaker: سفيان الثوري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r12.claim: Sufyan al-Thawri gives thirty-four years as the age of ashudd.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r12.anchor: أربع وثلاثون سنة قاله سفيان الثوري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r13.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r13.claim: Al-Suddi gives thirty years and suggests that the later marriage-age verse may have abrogated this ruling.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p148#2/r13.anchor: ثلاثون سنة قاله السدي وقال ثم جاء بعد هذه الآية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150/r1.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150/r1.claim: The author says the correct meaning of ashudd is puberty, as Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Shaʿbi, Yahya ibn Yaʿmar, Rabiʿa, and Malik hold.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150/r1.anchor: والثامن بلوغ الحلم قاله زيد بن أسلم والشعبي ويحيى بن يعمر وربيعة ومالك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150/r2.claim: The author doubts the earlier age reports belong here, suspecting compilers transferred them from the interpretation of 12:22; he distinguishes reaching full growth from its completion.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150/r2.anchor: ولا أظن بالذين حكينا عنهم الأقوال التي قبله فسروا هذه الآية بما ذكر عنهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150/r3.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150/r3.claim: Ibn Jarir supplies an ellipsis: protect the orphan’s property until maturity, then, once maturity and good judgment are found, deliver it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150/r3.anchor: حتى يبلغ أشده فإذا بلغ أشده فآنستم منه رشدا فادفعوا إليه ماله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150/r4.claim: The author rejects the claim that all this is already explicit in the verse: maturity and Islam are drawn from another verse, so an unqualified statement is limited by the qualified one.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150/r4.anchor: فليس بصحيح وإنما استفيد إيناس الرشد والإسلام من آية أخرى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150#2/r1.claim: Fulfill the measure and do not reduce it; qist means justice. A person is charged only within capacity.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150#2/r1.anchor: والقسط العدل ﴿ لا نكلف نفسا إلا وسعها ﴾ أي ما يسعها ولا تضيق عنه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150#2/r2.speaker: القاضي أبو يعلى
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150#2/r2.claim: Qadi Abu Yaʿla says exact infinitesimal precision is impossible in weighing and measuring, so one must strive carefully rather than guarantee perfection.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150#2/r2.anchor: يتعذر فيهما التحديد بأقل القليل كلفنا الاجتهاد في التحري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150#2/r3.claim: Speak or testify justly, telling the truth even when the person concerned is a relative; God’s covenant includes His commands and vows people impose on themselves.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150#2/r3.anchor: إذا تكلمتم أو شهدتم فقولوا الحق ولو كان المشهود له أو عليه ذا قرابة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150#2/r4.claim: The purpose of these instructions is that people remember and act on them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150#2/r4.anchor: وعهد الله يشتمل على ما عهده إلى الخلق وأوصاهم به وعلى ما أوجبه الإنسان على نفسه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150#2/r5.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150#2/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr read the listed forms of tadhakkur with a doubled dhāl.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150#2/r5.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو تذكرون ويذكرون ويذكر الإنسان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150#2/r6.speaker: نافع
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150#2/r6.claim: Nafiʿ, Abu Bakr from ʿAsim, and Ibn ʿAmir double the dhāl in all these forms except “does the human not remember,” which they lighten.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو بكر عن عاصم وابن عامر كل ذلك بالتشديد إلا قوله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150#2/r7.speaker: حمزة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150#2/r7.claim: Aban and Hafs from ʿAsim read yadhkurun with a light dhāl throughout; Hamza and al-Kisaʾi double it with yāʾ but lighten it with tāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p150#2/r7.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي يذكرون مشددا إذا كان بالياء ومخففا إذا كان بالتاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p363#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p363#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p363#2/r1.claim: After the orphan-property warning, caretakers separated the orphan's food and drink, but leftovers spoiled; the Prophet then received 2:220 permitting shared food and drink when managing orphans is for their good. Reported by Abū Dāwūd.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p363#2/r1.anchor: فانطلق من كان عنده يتيم فعزل طعامه من طعامه وشرابه من شرابه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p363#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p363#2/r2.speaker: الشعبي ومالك وغير واحد من السلف
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p363#2/r2.claim: The orphan reaches full maturity at puberty.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p363#2/r2.anchor: قال الشعبي، ومالك، وغير واحد من السلف: يعني: حتى يحتلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p363#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p363#2/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p363#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddī places the age of full maturity at thirty; other views say forty or sixty, which Ibn Kathīr judges remote in this context.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p363#2/r3.anchor: قال السدي: حتى يبلغ ثلاثين سنة، وقيل: أربعون سنة، وقيل: ستون سنة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p363#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p363#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p363#2/r4.claim: The proposed ages of thirty, forty, and sixty are all far-fetched for the maturity meant here.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p363#2/r4.anchor: وهذا كله بعيد هاهنا، والله أعلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p364/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p364/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p364/r1.claim: Fair dealing requires justice in both taking and giving; God threatened people who short measure or weight and destroyed a nation for cheating with measures and scales.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p364/r1.anchor: يأمر تعالى بإقامة العدل في الأخذ والإعطاء، كما توعد على تركه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p364/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p364/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p364/r2.claim: The Prophet warns those responsible for measuring and weighing that earlier nations perished through this responsibility; al-Tirmidhi says the raised report is known only through al-Ḥusayn ibn Qays, who is weak, while a sound version stops at Ibn ʿAbbās.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p364/r2.anchor: ثم قال: لا نعرفه مرفوعا إلا من حديث الحسين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p364/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p364/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p364/r3.claim: A second report says the community entrusted with measuring and weighing was given the two practices by which earlier generations perished.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p364/r3.anchor: إنكم معشر الموالي قد بشركم الله بخصلتين بها هلكت القرون المتقدمة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p364#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p364#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p364#2/r1.claim: Whoever makes a full effort to give and receive what is due is not blameworthy for an error after exhausting their ability.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p364#2/r1.anchor: من اجتهد في أداء الحق وأخذه، فإن أخطأ بعد استفراغ وسعه وبذل جهده فلا حرج عليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p364#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p364#2/r2.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p364#2/r2.claim: A person who measures and weighs fully with sincere intent is not held accountable; Ibn Kathīr calls this a rare disconnected report.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p364#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p364#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p364#2/r3.claim: Speech and action alike must be just toward relatives and strangers, at every time and in every circumstance.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p364#2/r3.anchor: يأمر تعالى بالعدل في الفعال والمقال، على القريب والبعيد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p365/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p365/r1.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p365/r1.claim: Fulfilling God's covenant means obeying what He commands and forbids and acting by His Book and the Messenger's Sunnah.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p365/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p365/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p365/r2.claim: The injunctions are emphasized so people may take heed and stop their former conduct; some recite the ذال in تذكرون with doubling and others without it.

JISHUMI:v4p2465/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2465/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2465/r3.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ read tadhakkarūn without doubling the dhāl; other readers double it throughout the Qur'an, with the same meaning.
JISHUMI:v4p2465/r3.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم تذكرون بالتخفيف، وقرأ الباقون تذكرون

JISHUMI:v4p2465/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2465/r4.speaker: علي بن عيسى
JISHUMI:v4p2465/r4.claim: Al-ashudd may be a plural of shiddah; other grammarians say it has no singular or is itself singular. It means a youth's developed strength, as in ʿAntara's line.
JISHUMI:v4p2465/r4.anchor: الأشد: قال علي بن عيسى جمع شد، كما أن الأصر جمع صر

JISHUMI:v4p2465/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2465/r5.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v4p2465/r5.claim: Abu Muslim parses al-ashudd as the plural of shiddah, like niʿmah/anʿum; qist means justice.
JISHUMI:v4p2465/r5.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم: الأشد جمع شدة مثل نعمة وأنعم

JISHUMI:v4p2465/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2465/r6.speaker: المفضل
JISHUMI:v4p2465/r6.claim: A line attributed through al-Mufaḍḍal uses شد النهار for the height or strength of daylight as evidence for al-ashudd.
JISHUMI:v4p2465/r6.anchor: قال عنترة: رواه المفضل: عهدي به شد النهار كأنما

JISHUMI:v4p2465/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2465/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2465/r7.claim: ذا قربى is the predicate of kāna with its subject omitted; awfaw and waffaw have the same meaning.
JISHUMI:v4p2465/r7.anchor: نصب ذا قربى على خبر (كان)، واسم (كان) محذوف

JISHUMI:v4p2466/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r1.claim: An orphan is a child without a father; the verse says not to approach the child's property except beneficially, emphasizing caution because the child cannot defend self or property.
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r1.anchor: ولا تقربوا يعني لا تتأولوا ولا تأخذوا، وإنما ذكر القرب تأكيدا

JISHUMI:v4p2466/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r2.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك والسدي
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r2.claim: ‘In the best manner’ can mean protecting the property until maturity or investing it through trade; other views allow customary guardian consumption, borrowing, or use of an animal or servant.
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r2.anchor: وقيل: هي حفظه إلى أن يكبر فيسلم المال إليه، وقيل: ينميه بالتجارة

JISHUMI:v4p2466/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r3.speaker: أبو علي وابن زيد
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r3.claim: A guardian may consume from the orphan's property according to custom, but this view excludes clothing.
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r3.anchor: وقيل: أكل القيم عليه بالمعروف دون الكسوة، عن أبي علي وابن زيد

JISHUMI:v4p2466/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r4.speaker: السدي
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r4.claim: Al-ashudd may mean thirty years; other reports give puberty, maturity around eighteen to thirty, or full strength.
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r4.anchor: وقيل: يحتلم فتكتب عليه الحسنات والسيئات عن يحيى بن [يعمر والشعبي]

JISHUMI:v4p2466/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r5.claim: Abu Hanifa sets al-ashudd at twenty-five; the judge instead selects when a youth can protect the property, which the author says reflects the purpose of the limit.
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r5.anchor: عن أبي حنيفة، وقيل: حتى يتقوى على حفظ [ماله]

JISHUMI:v4p2466/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r6.claim: Reaching full strength alone does not require handing over property; the implied condition is that sound judgment also be evident so the orphan can preserve it.
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r6.anchor: وفي الآية حذف؛ لأن مجرد بلوغ الأشد لا يوجب دفع ماله إليه

JISHUMI:v4p2466/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r7.claim: The capacity clause excuses unavoidable tiny errors in measure or weight; another gloss is that God assigns only what is manageable and lawful.
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r7.anchor: قيل: في إيفاء الكيل والوزن، حتى لا يؤاخذ في ذلك بالحبات

JISHUMI:v4p2466/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r8.claim: ‘When you speak, be just’ requires truth in testimony, speech, wills, enjoining right, legal opinions, judgments, rulings, and schools of thought.
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r8.anchor: وهذا من الأوامر العجيبة البليغة التي يعقل فيها مع قلة حروفها

JISHUMI:v4p2466/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r9.claim: Even if the person judged or testified about is a relative, kinship must not prevent truthful speech.
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r9.anchor: فلا تمنعن قرابته أن تقولوا الصدق

JISHUMI:v4p2466/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r10.claim: God's covenant includes obligations, the commands in these verses, oaths, and what one binds oneself to; the author says all are intended, while Ibn ʿAbbas calls these rulings clear and unabrogated.
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r10.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: أن هذه آيات محكمات لم ينسخ منها شيء

JISHUMI:v4p2466/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r11.speaker: كعب
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r11.claim: Kaʿb says these verses open the Torah; al-Rabiʿ ibn Khuthaym compares them to a page bearing Muhammad's seal.
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r11.anchor: وعن كعب: أول التوراة هذه الآيات، وعن الربيع بن خثيم

JISHUMI:v4p2466/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r12.claim: The closing purpose may be remembering, taking admonition, avoiding neglect, reflecting on duties, recalling punishment, or becoming people of remembrance.
JISHUMI:v4p2466/r12.anchor: وقيل: كي لا تغفلوا عنه، وتتركوا العمل به، وقيل:

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r5.claim: The commands and prohibitions share the opening ruling; it prohibits their opposites, including mistreating parents, short measures, unjust speech, and breaking the covenant.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p74#3/r5.anchor: علم أن التحريم راجع إلى أضدادها ، وهي الإساءة إلى الوالدين ، وبخس الكيل والميزان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p75/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p75/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p75/r1.claim: The best handling of an orphan’s property is to preserve and grow it until maturity, then hand it over.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p75/r1.anchor: إلا بالخصلة التي هي أحسن ما يفعل بمال اليتيم ، وهي حفظه وتثميره

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p75/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p75/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p75/r2.claim: By fairness means accurate equality; God burdens no soul beyond its capacity.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p75/r2.anchor: السوية والعدل ؛ { لا نكلف نفسا إلا وسعها } إلا ما يسعها ولا تعجز عنه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p75/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p75/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p75/r3.claim: The capacity qualification follows exact measurement because staying precisely at the just limit may be difficult; one must reach ability and is excused beyond it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p75/r3.anchor: لأن مراعاة الحد من القسط الذي لا زيادة فيه ولا نقصان مما يجري فيه الحرج

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p75/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p75/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p75/r4.claim: Speak justly in testimony about relatives without adding or withholding, as 4:135 likewise commands.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p75/r4.anchor: ولو كان المقول له أو عليه في شهادة أو غيرها من أهل قرابة القاتل

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r1.claim: The orphan's property is singled out because weak oversight makes it especially tempting, although other people's property is equally protected.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r1.anchor: إنما خص مال اليتيم بالذكر وإن كان مال غيره في التحريم بمثابته , لأن الطمع فيه لقلة مراعيه أقوى

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r2.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r2.claim: The best treatment is preserving the ward's property until the ward is grown and can receive it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r2.anchor: حفظ ماله عليه إلى أن يكبر ليتسلمه , قاله الكلبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r3.claim: The best treatment is investing the property in trade.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r3.anchor: أن ذلك هو التجارة به , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r4.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r4.claim: A guardian who trades with the property should not take any of its profits.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r4.anchor: هو ألا يأخذ من الربح إذا اتجر له بالمال شيئا , قاله الضحاك

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r5.claim: A poor guardian may consume a customary amount, but a rich guardian should abstain and neither take clothing nor anything else.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r5.anchor: أن يأكل الولي بالمعروف من ماله إن افتقر , ويترك إن استغنى

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r6.claim: The best treatment may be preserving the principal while growing its returns.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r6.anchor: أن التي هي أحسن : حفظ أصوله وتثمير فروعه

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r7.claim: A ward reaches maturity at strength and youth; reported thresholds are puberty, thirty years, or eighteen years.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r7.anchor: الأشد القوة والشباب . وفي حدها ثلاثة أقاويل : أحدها : أنه الحلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r8.speaker: ربيعة وزيد بن أسلم ومالك
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r8.claim: The age of maturity is puberty, when good and bad deeds begin to be recorded.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r8.anchor: أنه الحلم حين تكتب له الحسنات وعليه السيئات

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r9.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r9.claim: The age of maturity is thirty years.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r9.anchor: أن الأشد ثلاثون سنة , قاله السدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r10.speaker: علي بن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r10.claim: The age of maturity is eighteen years.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r10.anchor: أن الأشد ثماني عشرة سنة , ذكره علي بن عيسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r11.claim: Give full measure and weight fairly, applying to a seller's property the same fairness required with an orphan's property.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r11.anchor: يعني بالعدل , أمر في مال البائع من تأدية بمثل ما أمر به في مال اليتيم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r12.claim: Since exactness at the tiniest degree is impossible, what lies beyond ability is excused and not required.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r12.anchor: وكان تحديد أقل القليل متعذرا , كان ذلك عفوا , لأنه لا يدخل في الوسع

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r13.claim: “When you speak, be just” may require fairness in judgment, truth in testimony, or impartiality in mediation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r13.anchor: أحدها : إذا حكمتم فأنصفوا . الثاني : إذا شهدتم فاصدقوا

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r14.claim: God's covenant may be any obligation a person undertakes, such as a vow, or an oath by God that must be kept unless sinful.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r14.anchor: أن عهد الله كل ما أوجبه الإنسان على نفسه من نذر وغيره

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r15.claim: “That is what He enjoined” may refer to the commands given to the Jews in the Torah or to Muslims in the Qur'an.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p187/r15.anchor: أنه راجع إلى الذين هادوا وما أوصاهم به في التوراة

MUQATIL:6:151-152#2/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:151-152#2/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:151-152#2/r1.claim: Orphan property may be used only to grow it through profit until the orphan reaches eighteen; fulfill measures and weights fairly and within each person’s capacity.
MUQATIL:6:151-152#2/r1.anchor: إلا ليثمر لليتيم ماله بالأرباح، { حتى يبلغ أشده } ، يعني ثماني عشرة سنة،

MUQATIL:6:151-152#2/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:151-152#2/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:151-152#2/r2.claim: Speak justly even about relatives and fulfill God’s covenant with people; these commands and prohibitions are meant to prompt remembrance.
MUQATIL:6:151-152#2/r2.anchor: يعنى أولى قربى إذا تكلمتم فقولوا الحق، وإن كان ذو قرابتك فقل فيه الحق،

NASAFI-FULL:v1p352#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352#2/r1.claim: The best way to approach an orphan's property is to protect and grow it.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352#2/r1.anchor: إلا بالخصلة التى هى أحسن وهي حفظه وتثميره

NASAFI-FULL:v1p352#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352#2/r2.claim: Reaching full strength means attaining puberty; then the property is delivered. Shadd is a singular form like fals.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352#2/r2.anchor: مبلغ حلمه فادفعوه إليه وواحده شد كفلس وأفلس

NASAFI-FULL:v1p352#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352#2/r3.claim: Fair measure and weight means equality and justice; the following capacity limit excuses unavoidable difficulty in observing the precise margin.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352#2/r3.anchor: ﴿ وأوفوا الكيل والميزان بالقسط ﴾ بالسوية والعدل ﴿ لا نكلف نفسا إلا وسعها ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v1p352#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352#2/r4.claim: God requires only what a person can bear; anything beyond the attainable measure is excused because exact limits may be burdensome.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352#2/r4.anchor: وإنما اتبع الأمر بإيفاء الكيل والميزان ذلك لأن مراعاة الحد من القسط الذى لا زيادة ولا نقصان مما فيه حرج

NASAFI-FULL:v1p352#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352#2/r5.claim: When speaking or judging, be truthful and just even where a relative is concerned, whether in testimony or otherwise.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352#2/r5.anchor: ﴿ وإذا قلتم فاعدلوا ﴾ فأصدقوا ﴿ ولو كان ذا قربى ﴾ ولو كان المقوم له أو عليه فى شهادة أو غيرها

NASAFI-FULL:v1p352#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352#2/r6.claim: God's covenant may be the primordial covenant or His commands, prohibitions, promise and threat, vows, and oaths; all are to be fulfilled.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352#2/r6.anchor: يوم الميثاق أو فى الأمر والنهى والوعد والوعيد والنذر واليمين

NASAFI-FULL:v1p352#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352#2/r7.claim: Ḥamza, ʿAlī, and Ḥafṣ read the form with one tāʾ omitted; others geminate it through assimilation, meaning take heed.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p352#2/r7.anchor: بالتخفيف حيث كان حمزة وعلى وحفص على حذف إحدى التاءين

QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r2.claim: Approach an orphan's property only in the way best for the orphan, by protecting its principal and growing its returns; Qurtubi prefers this as the most comprehensive interpretation.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r2.anchor: وهذا أحسن الأقوال في هذا فإنه جامع

QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r3.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r3.claim: Mujahid interprets the permitted approach as trading with the orphan's property, while forbidding buying from or borrowing it.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد: { ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم إلا بالتي هي أحسن }

QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r4.claim: An orphan's “maturity” requires both bodily strength and experiential understanding; the unrestricted wording is clarified by 4:6, which joins reaching marriageable age with sound judgment.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r5.claim: If an orphan receives property after physical maturity but before sound judgment, he may squander it on desires and be left destitute.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r5.anchor: فلو مكن اليتيم من ماله قبل حصول المعرفة وبعد حصول القوة لأذهبه في شهواته

QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r6.claim: The orphan is singled out because people neglect him and his father is absent; attending to one who has lost a father merits special care, and God is the orphan's adversary against an abuser.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r6.anchor: وخص اليتيم بهذا الشرط لغفلة الناس عنه وافتقاد الآباء لأبنائهم

QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r7.claim: Even after reaching maturity, an orphan's property may only be approached in the best way; the verse implies that once maturity and sound judgment are seen, his property is to be handed over.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r7.anchor: وليس بلوغ الأشد يبيح قرب ماله بغير الأحسن لأن الحرمة في حق البالغ ثابتة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the orphan's “maturity” with reaching puberty.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r8.anchor: فقال ابن زيد: بلوغه وقال أهل المدينة.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r9.speaker: أهل المدينة
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r9.claim: The people of Medina require both puberty and evidence of sound judgment for an orphan's maturity.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r9.anchor: وقال أهل المدينة. بلوغه وإيناس رشده

QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r10.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r10.claim: Abu Hanifa sets the orphan's age of maturity at twenty-five.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r10.anchor: وعند أبي حنيفة: خمس وعشرون سنة.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r11.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r11.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi objects that Abu Hanifa disallows establishing fixed measures by analogy or reasoning yet fixes this age using weak reports; he sharply contrasts Abu Hanifa's surroundings with Malik's scholarly environment.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152/r11.anchor: قال ابن العربي: وعجبا من أبي حنيفة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r1.claim: Some say the age of full strength culminates at the end of mature adulthood, citing Suhaym ibn Wathil's line about a man of fifty whose strength is gathered.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r1.anchor: أخو خمسين مجتمع أشدي ونجذني مداورة الشؤون

QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r2.claim: “Ashudd” has no singular in one account, like “al-ānuk” (lead); alternatives give “shadd” or “shiddah,” and lexical authorities disagree over whether these are attested forms or only analogy.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r2.anchor: والأشد واحد لا جمع له بمنزلة الآنك

QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r3.claim: The word is connected with the rising intensity of daytime, as in “the height of the day”; Muhammad al-Dabbi recited ʿAntara's line as evidence for “shadd al-nahar.”
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r3.anchor: وأصله من شد النهار أي ارتفع

QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r4.claim: A second poet's line uses “shadd al-nahar” for the time when a woman passes by; it is another usage supporting the expression.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r4.anchor: وكان محمد بن محمد الضبي ينشد بيت عنترة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r5.speaker: سيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r5.claim: Sibawayh says the singular is “shiddah”; al-Jawhari finds this semantically apt but notes that the plural pattern does not normally pluralize a faʿlah noun as afʿul.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r6.claim: Forms such as “shadd” for “ashudd” are analogical rather than heard from Arabic usage, like the proposed singular “ibul” for “ababil”; Abu Zayd also records “shadā” for hardship and “ashadda” for possessing a strong riding animal.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r6.anchor: وليس هو شيئا سمع من العرب

QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r7.claim: Fulfilling measure and weight justly means giving and receiving accurately in sales; “qist” means justice.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r7.anchor: أي بالاعتدال في الأخذ والعطاء عند البيع

QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r8.claim: The capacity qualification excuses unavoidable variations between measures, since people are accountable only for care and precision within human control.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r8.anchor: وهذا يقتضي أن هذه الأوامر إنما هي فيما يقع تحت قدرة البشر من التحفظ والتحرر

QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r9.claim: Some take “measure” to mean the measuring vessel itself, which explains its pairing with the scale.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r10.claim: Some scholars say the seller is required to give exactly what is owed, not extra, and the creditor to accept exactly what is owed, not less, so neither is burdened with resentment.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r10.anchor: أمر المعطي بإيفاء رب الحق حقه الذي هو له

QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r11.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r11.claim: A report reaching Ibn ʿAbbas says public embezzlement brings fear, widespread adultery death, short measure and weight loss of provision, unjust rule bloodshed, and treachery in covenants an enemy's domination.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r11.anchor: ما ظهر الغلول في قوم قط إلا ألقى الله

QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r12.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas warns non-Arabs that the two practices which ruined earlier peoples were measure and weight.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r12.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا: إنكم معشر الأعاجم

QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r13.claim: The command to speak justly covers legal judgments and testimony, even where the truth goes against relatives.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r13.anchor: ولو كان الحق على مثل قراباتكم

QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r14.claim: Fulfilling God's covenant is general for all obligations He gave His servants; it may also include agreements between people, called God's covenant because He commands that they be kept.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:152-153/r14.anchor: ويحتمل أن يراد به جميع ما انعقد بين إنسانين

RAZI-FULL:v13p192/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p192/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p192/r1.claim: The preceding verse lists five evident duties needing little thought; this verse adds four subtle duties whose measure requires reflection and effort.
RAZI-FULL:v13p192/r1.anchor: اعلم أنه تعالى ذكر في الآية الأولى خمسة أنواع من التكاليف ، وهي أمور ظاهرة جلية

RAZI-FULL:v13p192/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p192/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p192/r2.claim: An orphan's property may be approached only for its best interest, including investment and profit; a needy guardian may take a reasonable amount, while a rich guardian should abstain.
RAZI-FULL:v13p192/r2.anchor: ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم إلا بأن يسعى في تنميته وتحصيل الربح به ورعاية وجوه الغبطة له

RAZI-FULL:v13p192/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p192/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p192/r3.claim: Protect the orphan's property until maturity, then deliver it; maturity is interpreted as puberty together with discernible sound judgment.
RAZI-FULL:v13p192/r3.anchor: احفظوا ماله حتى يبلغ أشده ، فإذا بلغ أشده فادفعوا إليه ماله .

RAZI-FULL:v13p192/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p192/r4.speaker: الليث
RAZI-FULL:v13p192/r4.claim: Al-Layth defines reaching maturity as attaining adult wisdom and knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v13p192/r4.anchor: قال الليث : الأشد . مبلغ الرجل الحكمة والمعرفة .

RAZI-FULL:v13p192/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p192/r5.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v13p192/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the singular of ashudd would analogically be shadd, but he had not heard a singular form.
RAZI-FULL:v13p192/r5.anchor: قال الفراء : الأشد . وأحدها شد في القياس ، ولم أسمع لها بواحد .

RAZI-FULL:v13p192/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p192/r6.speaker: أبو الهيثم
RAZI-FULL:v13p192/r6.claim: Abū al-Haytham gives shiddah as the singular and explains it as strength and toughness.
RAZI-FULL:v13p192/r6.anchor: وقال أبو الهيثم : واحدة الأشد شدة كما أن واحدة الأنعم نعمة ، والشدة : القوة والجلادة

RAZI-FULL:v13p192/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p192/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p192/r7.claim: Fulfilling a measure means completing it without shortfall; the scale clause means weighing justly, with no fraud or reduction.
RAZI-FULL:v13p192/r7.anchor: وأوفى الكيل إذا أتمه ولم ينقص منه شيئا

RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r1.claim: The seller must give the rights-holder the full due, while the buyer must take only the due and not demand extra; these are the complementary meanings of just measurement.
RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r1.anchor: أمر الله المعطي بإيفاء ذي الحق حقه من غير نقصاه ، وأمر صاحب الحق بأخذ حقه من غير طلب الزيادة

RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r2.claim: The command requires only the measure and weight a person can reasonably achieve, not unattainable exactness.
RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r2.anchor: الواجب في إيفاء الكيل والوزن هذا القدر الممكن في إيفاء الكيل والوزن . أما التحقيق فغير واجب . قال القاضي

RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r3.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r3.claim: Al-Qāḍī argues that if God eases the attainable duty of exact measurement, it is incoherent to claim He obliges faith from an incapable unbeliever while creating and willing that person's disbelief.
RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r3.anchor: قال القاضي : إذا كان تعالى قد خفف على المكلف هذا التخفيف مع أن ما هو التضييق مقدور له

RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r4.claim: The author answers al-Qāḍī and his teachers by invoking divine knowledge and the motive, saying their argument loses its force there.
RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r4.anchor: واعلم أنا نعارض القاضي وشيوخه في هذا الموضع بمسألة العلم ومسألة الداعي

RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r5.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r5.claim: The commentators restrict the command to speaking justly to testimony or commands and prohibitions.
RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r5.anchor: والمفسرون حملوه على أداء الشهادة فقط ، والأمر والنهي فقط ، قال القاضي وليس الأمر كذلك

RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r6.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r6.claim: Al-Qāḍī reads the command broadly: religious preaching and argument should be concise and understandable, and enjoining right must avoid both excess harm and falling short of duty.
RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r6.anchor: قال القاضي وليس الأمر كذلك بل يدخل فيه كل ما يتصل بالقول

RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r7.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r7.claim: The broad command also requires accurate narratives and transmission of others' messages without additions or omissions, and fairness in a judge's spoken ruling.
RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r7.anchor: ومن جملتها تبليغ الرسالات عن الناس ، فإنه يجب أن يؤديها من غير زيادة ولا نقصان

RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r8.claim: Speech must be fair to kin and stranger alike, since the aim is God's approval and does not vary with the relationship.
RAZI-FULL:v13p192#2/r8.anchor: يجب أن يسوي فيه بين القريب والبعيد ، لأنه لما كان المقصود منه طلب رضوان الله تعالى لم يختلف ذلك بالقريب والبعيد

RAZI-FULL:v13p193/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p193/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p193/r1.claim: Fulfilling God's covenant is a subtle duty because a person may swear privately and keep or break that oath without others knowing.
RAZI-FULL:v13p193/r1.anchor: وهذا من خفيات الأمور لأن الرجل قد يحلف مع نفسه ، فيكون ذلك الحلف خفيا ، ويكون بره وحنثه أيضا خفيا

RAZI-FULL:v13p193/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p193/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p193/r2.claim: The first verse ends with understanding because its five duties are evident; this verse ends with remembrance because its four subtle duties require thought to find the balanced course.
RAZI-FULL:v13p193/r2.anchor: قلنا : لأن التكاليف الخمسة المذكورة في الأولى أمور ظاهرة جلية ، فوجب تعقلها وتفهمها

RAZI-FULL:v13p193/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p193/r3.speaker: حمزة
RAZI-FULL:v13p193/r3.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read tadhakkarūn with a lightened dhāl; the other readers double it, with no difference in meaning.
RAZI-FULL:v13p193/r3.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم { تذكرون } بالتخفيف والباقون { * تذكرن } بتشديد الذال

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r1.claim: إلا بالتي هي أحسن is an exceptive construction meaning only by the best course; it may be circumstantial or an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, and the comparative urges the best rather than merely good.
