SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r1.anchor: استثناء مفرغ أي: لا تقربوه إلا بالخصلة الحسنى، فيجوز أن يكون حالا، وأن يكون نعت مصدر

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r2.claim: حتى يبلغ is a semantic endpoint for protecting the orphan's property; a literal endpoint would wrongly imply that one should then approach it.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r2.anchor: هذه غاية من حيث المعنى فإن المعنى: احفظوا ما له حتى يبلغ أشده ولو/ جعلناه غاية للفظ

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r3.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r3.claim: He says الأشد has no attested singular, though قياس would give شد.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r3.anchor: هو جمع لا واحد له، وهو قول الفراء فإنه قال: " الأشد واحدها " شد " في القياس ولم أسمع لها بواحد

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r4.claim: He transmits a view from some language authorities that الأشد is singular, comparable to الآنك.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r4.anchor: وقيل: هو مفرد لا جمع، نقل ابن الأنباري عن بعض أهل اللغة ذلك، وأنه بمنزلة الآنك

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r5.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r5.claim: He rejects the singular analysis because أفعل is not established as a singular noun pattern.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r5.anchor: وليس بمختار لفقدان أفعل في المفردات وضعا

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r6.speaker: أبو الهيثم
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r6.claim: He treats الأشد as a plural of شدة, with the feminine ending considered extra before pluralization on أفعل.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r6.anchor: وقيل: هو جمع " شدة " ، وفعلة يجمع على أفعل كنعمة وأنعم، قاله أبو الهيثم

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r7.speaker: ابن الأنباري
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r7.claim: He transmits a Basran view that الأشد is the plural of شد with a damma on شين, like ود and أود.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r7.anchor: وقيل: هو جمع شد بضم الشين نقله ابن الأنباري عن بعض البصريين

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r8.claim: Another possible analysis makes الأشد a plural of شد with a fatha on شين.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r8.anchor: وقيل: هو جمع شد بفتحها وهو محتمل. والمراد هنا ببلوغ الأشد بلوغ الحلم

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r9.claim: Most interpreters take reaching الأشد here to mean puberty; other reported thresholds include mature skill, ages fifteen to thirty, thirty-three, forty, or sixty, though forty and sixty suit 46:15 instead.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r9.anchor: والمراد هنا ببلوغ الأشد بلوغ الحلم في قول الأكثر لأنه مظنة ذلك. وقيل: هو مبلغ الرجال

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r10.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r10.claim: He derives الأشد from شدة, strength and endurance, and cites poetry using it for maturity.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r10.anchor:
والأشد: مشتق من الشدة وهي القوة والجلادة، وأنشد الفراء:
2120 قد ساد وهو فتى

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r11.speaker: عنترة
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r11.claim: He gives an alternative derivation from rising or height, as in شد النهار, and cites a line.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153/r11.anchor:
وقيل: أصله من الارتفاع، من شد النهار إذا ارتفع وعلا، قال عنترة:
2121 عهدي به شد النهار

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#2/r1.claim: الكيل first names the act of measuring and then the measuring vessel; الميزان is the instrument pattern مفعال from weighing, with origin موزان changed like ميقات.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#2/r1.anchor: والكيل والميزان: هما الآلة التي يكال بها ويوزن، وأصل الكيل المصدر ثم أطلق على الآلة

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#2/r2.claim: بالقسط may describe the doer as acting justly or the measures as being made complete and fair.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#2/r2.anchor: و " بالقسط " حال من فاعل " أوفوا " أي: أوفوهما مقسطين أي: ملتبسين بالقسط

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#2/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#2/r3.claim: He treats الكيل and الميزان as verbal nouns meaning measured goods and proposes omitted nouns for the constructions.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#2/r3.anchor: والكيل هنا مصدر في معنى المكيل، وكذلك الميزان. ويجوز أن يكون فيه حذف مضاف

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#2/r4.claim: The author sees no need for Abu al-Baqa's substitutions because the meaning works directly; الكيل itself can mean the measuring vessel.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#2/r4.anchor: والظاهر عدم الاحتياج إلى ذلك وكأنه لم يعرف أن الكيل يطلق على نفس المكيال

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#2/r5.speaker: الواحدي
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#2/r5.claim: He understands الوفاء as completing the weighing, like completing the measure, and proposes an omitted noun with الميزان.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#2/r5.anchor: فإنه قال: " والميزان أي: وزن الميزان لأن المراد إتمام الوزن لا إتمام الميزان

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#2/r6.claim: The author rejects the omission analysis: the verse can speak directly of filling the measure because الكيل also names the vessel.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#2/r6.anchor: ولا حاجة إلى ما ادعاه من وقوع المصدر موقع اسم المفعول ولا من تقدير المضاف

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#3/r1.claim: لا نكلف is parenthetical between the commands; ولو كان ذو قربى means whether the person spoken to or spoken about is a relative.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#3/r1.anchor: قوله { لا نكلف } معترض بين هذه الأوامر، وقوله " ولو كان " أي: ولو كان المقول له والمقول عليه

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#3/r2.claim: عهد الله may be a possessive construction where God is the covenanting subject, or where He is its object, as in the cited verses.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#3/r2.anchor: وقوله " وبعهد الله " يجوز أن يكون من باب إضافة المصدر لفاعله أي: بما عاهدكم الله عليه،

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#3/r3.claim: A third reading treats the possessive as explanatory: the covenant is attributed to God because He commands its preservation.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#3/r3.anchor: وأن تكون الإضافة لمجرد البيان أضيف إلى الله من حيث إنه الآمر بحفظه

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#3/r4.claim: The ending with remembrance suits the four less obvious instructions that need thought to discern fairness; the other five are evident to reason and understanding.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#3/r4.anchor: وختمت هذه بالتذكر لأن الأربعة قبلها خفية تحتاج إلى إعمال فكر ونظر حتى يقف متعاطيها على العدل

SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#3/r5.claim: The two reciters and Hafs from Asim lighten تتذكرون by deleting one ت, while the others double it by assimilation; scholars differ which ت is deleted.
SAMIN-DURR:6:152-153#3/r5.anchor: وتذكرون حيث وقع يقرؤه الأخوان وعاصم في رواية حفص بالتخفيف، والباقون بالتشديد

STUDYQURAN:6:151/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r14.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r14.claim: A guardian must keep an orphan's property in trust until knowledge and wisdom mature; maturity is qualitative rather than a fixed age.
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r14.anchor: a guardian should hold the orphan’s property in trust until the orphan reaches the age when knowledge and wisdom are sufficiently developed (R)—a standard that is qualitative

STUDYQURAN:6:151/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r15.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r15.claim: One view allows an impoverished guardian to take a small amount from the orphan's property, provided it is repaid when possible.
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r15.anchor: when he is able, or to the guardian’s right to use the orphan’s property in a way that might help maintain or improve it (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:6:151/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r16.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r16.claim: Alternatively, the guardian may use orphan property in a way that maintains or improves its value.
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r16.anchor: the guardian’s right to use the orphan’s property in a way that might help maintain or improve it (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:6:151/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r17.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r17.claim: Giving full measure and weight justly requires fairness and probity in commerce and business.
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r17.anchor: To observe fully the measure and the balance with justice refers to the requirement to engage in commerce and business transactions with probity and fairness

STUDYQURAN:6:151/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r18.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r18.claim: God's not burdening a soul beyond its capacity is a central Islamic doctrine repeated elsewhere.

STUDYQURAN:6:151/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r19.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r19.claim: Speaking just includes truthful testimony and integrity and truthfulness in all speech.
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r19.anchor: refers to the importance of truthful testimony, but also to the requirement that one speak with integrity and truthfulness at all times (R)

STUDYQURAN:6:151/r20.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r20.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r20.claim: The Quran also commands honorable speech and justice in speech; this verse requires impartial justice even when the truth is against a relative.
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r20.anchor: the injunction in v. 152 requires that one speak justly even if it be [against] a kinsman

STUDYQURAN:6:151/r21.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r21.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r21.claim: Fulfilling God's pact here means obeying the commands and prohibitions God established.
STUDYQURAN:6:151/r21.anchor: in the present verse, it is understood to mean obeying the injunctions and prohibitions established by God (Ṭ)

ZAJJAJ:v2p304/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p304/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ZAJJAJ:v2p304/r5.claim: Some say the best use of an orphan’s property is to ride his animal and use his servant; the author says the wording does not indicate that.
ZAJJAJ:v2p304/r5.anchor:
قال بعضهم: التي هي أحسن ركوب دابته واستخدام خادمه، وليس في
الظاهر أن هذا هو المراد،

ZAJJAJ:v2p304/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p304/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p304/r6.claim: The best treatment means preserving and increasing the orphan’s property by whatever available means.
ZAJJAJ:v2p304/r6.anchor:
وإنما التي هي أحسن حفظ ماله عليه، وتثميره
بما وجد إليه السبيل.

ZAJJAJ:v2p305/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p305/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p305/r1.claim: حتى is understood from the sense: preserve the orphan’s property until maturity, then deliver it; maturity requires adulthood and sound judgment.
ZAJJAJ:v2p305/r1.anchor:
حتى " محمولة على المعنى، المعنى احفظوه عليه حتى يبلغ أشده.
أي فإذا بلغ أشده فادفعوه إليه.

ZAJJAJ:v2p305/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p305/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ZAJJAJ:v2p305/r2.claim: Some define maturity as eighteen years; the author rejects this because a ward who reaches adulthood earlier and shows sound judgment must receive his property.
ZAJJAJ:v2p305/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم: (حتى يبلغ أشده) حتى يبلغ ثماني عشرة سنة، ولست أعرف ما وجه ذلك

ZAJJAJ:v2p305/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p305/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p305/r3.claim: When you speak, judge, or testify, act justly even if the person concerned is a relative.
ZAJJAJ:v2p305/r3.anchor: أي إذا شهدتم أو حكمتم فاعدلوا، ولو كان المشهود عليه أو له ذا قربى.

TABATABAI:6:151-152/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151-152/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:151-152/r7.claim: Prohibiting even approaching an orphan's property covers consumption, use, and every disposition; only the best means of safeguarding it is allowed until the orphan reaches maturity.
TABATABAI:6:151-152/r7.anchor: النهي عن القرب للدلالة على التعميم فلا يحل أكل ماله ولا استعماله

TABATABAI:6:151-152/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151-152/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:151-152/r8.claim: Reaching mature strength means attaining puberty and sound judgment, as the instruction to test orphans and give them property when they reach marriage age and show good judgment confirms.
TABATABAI:6:151-152/r8.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن المراد ببلوغه أشده هو البلوغ والرشد كما يدل عليه أيضا قوله

TABATABAI:6:152/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:152/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:152/r1.claim: The maturity limit does not newly permit others to handle the property; it marks when guardianship is no longer needed because the owner can manage and develop it himself.
TABATABAI:6:152/r1.anchor: ويظهر أيضا أنه ليس المراد بتحديد حرمة التصرف في مال اليتيم بقوله { حتى يبلغ أشده } رفع الحرمة

TABATABAI:6:152/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:152/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:152/r2.claim: Giving full measure and weight fairly means acting justly without shortchanging.
TABATABAI:6:152/r2.anchor: الإيفاء بالقسط هو العمل بالعدل فيهما من غير بخس

TABATABAI:6:152/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:152/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:152/r3.claim: The statement that God burdens no soul beyond capacity answers the concern that perfectly exact justice is impossible in ordinary transactions; the attainable standard is required and may apply to both orphan-property care and fair measures.
TABATABAI:6:152/r3.anchor: وقوله { لا نكلف نفسا إلا وسعها } بمنزلة دفع الدخل

TABATABAI:6:152-153/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:152-153/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:152-153/r1.claim: Justice in speech concerns statements that can benefit or harm others, especially matters of rights such as testimony, judgments, and legal opinions; affection must not distort testimony or rulings for relatives.
TABATABAI:6:152-153/r1.anchor: فالمعنى وراقبوا أقوالكم التي فيها نفع أو ضرر للناس واعدلوا فيها

TABATABAI:6:152-153/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:152-153/r2.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:6:152-153/r2.claim: Al-Majma' says this concise command includes confessions, testimony, wills, legal opinions, cases, rulings, doctrinal positions, and enjoining right or forbidding wrong.
TABATABAI:6:152-153/r2.anchor: قال في المجمع وهذا من الأوامر البليغة التي يدخل فيها مع قلة حروفها

TABATABAI:6:152-153/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:152-153/r3.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:6:152-153/r3.claim: Al-Raghib defines covenant as preserving and attending to something continually; the word can denote divine ordinances, assigned duties, agreements, vows, or oaths.
TABATABAI:6:152-153/r3.anchor: قال الراغب في المفردات العهد حفظ الشيء ومراعاته حالا بعد حال

TABATABAI:6:152-153/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:152-153/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:152-153/r4.claim: Given Qur'anic usage and the context of divine commands, fulfilling God's covenant most likely means carrying out religious obligations, though a pledge made to God remains possible.
TABATABAI:6:152-153/r4.anchor: كل ذلك يؤيد أن يكون المراد بقوله { وبعهد الله أوفوا } التكاليف الدينية الإلهية

TABATABAI:6:152-153/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:152-153/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:152-153/r5.claim: The covenant command is reinforced by the verse's closing reminder formula.
TABATABAI:6:152-153/r5.anchor: ثم أكد التكاليف المذكورة في الآية بقوله { ذلكم وصاكم به لعلكم تذكرون }

TABATABAI:6:151-157/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:151-157/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:151-157/r2.claim: The second verse's duties require reflection on shared social interests and the damage caused by neglecting the weak, cheating measures, unjust decisions, and suppressing truth; hence it ends with a call to remember.
TABATABAI:6:151-157/r2.anchor: يحتاج الإنسان مع تعبيه بالعقل في إدراك حالها إلى التذكر

TABRISI:6:152-153/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:152-153/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:152-153/r1.claim: Kufan readers except Abū Bakr lighten the dhāl in tadhakkarūn; others double it. The light form deletes the first tāʾ from the underlying tatadhakkarūn, while the doubled form assimilates the second tāʾ into dhāl.
TABRISI:6:152-153/r1.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة إلا أبا بكر تذكرون بتخفيف الذال حيث وقع والباقون بالتشديد

TABRISI:6:152-153/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:152-153/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:152-153/r5.claim: Ashudd can be a singular or plural, meaning the firm strength of youth and age; some derive it from shidda, while one Basran account treats it as a singular like al-ānuk. Dhikr and dhakar share a meaning; doubling the verb makes it take two objects.
TABRISI:6:152-153/r5.anchor: الأشد واحدها شد مثل الأشر في جمع شر والأضر في جمع ضر والشد القوة وهو استحكام قوة الشباب

TABRISI:6:152-153/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:152-153/r6.speaker: سيبويه
TABRISI:6:152-153/r6.claim: Sībawayh says the noun dhikr and dhakar have the same meaning; the verse’s doubled verb is causative, and tadhakkara is the reflexive counterpart, as a poetic example illustrates.
TABRISI:6:152-153/r6.anchor: قال سيبويه الذكر والذكر بمعنى وذكر فعل يتعدى إلى مفعول واحد

TABRISI:6:152-153/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:152-153/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:6:152-153/r7.claim: Mujāhid, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and al-Suddī say the guardian may develop the orphan’s property through trade.
TABRISI:6:152-153/r7.anchor: إلا بتثمير ماله بالتجارة عن مجاهد والضحاك والسدي

TABRISI:6:152-153/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:152-153/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
TABRISI:6:152-153/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd and al-Jubbāʾī permit the guardian to take customary food from the orphan’s property, but not clothing.
TABRISI:6:152-153/r8.anchor: بأن يأخذ القيم عليه بالأكل بالمعروف دون الكسوة عن ابن زيد والجبائي

TABRISI:6:152-153/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:152-153/r9.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:6:152-153/r9.claim: A further view says to preserve the orphan’s property until the child grows up.
TABRISI:6:152-153/r9.anchor: وثالثها: بأن يحفظ عليه حتى يكبر

TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r1.speaker: الشعبي
TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r1.claim: The orphan reaches ashudd at puberty, according to al-Shaʿbī; another view sets it at eighteen, while al-Suddī says thirty and considers that limit abrogated by 4:6.
TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r1.anchor: وقيل: هو أن يبلغ ثماني عشرة سنة وقال السدي: هو أن يبلغ ثلاثين سنة ثم نسخها قوله

TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r2.speaker: أبو حنيفة
TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r2.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa says the property is given to the orphan at twenty-five; before then, it is withheld if sound judgment has not been established.
TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r2.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: إذا بلغ خمسا وعشرين سنة دفع المال إليه

TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r3.claim: The strongest view sets no fixed age: the person must reach adulthood, mature mentally, and show sound judgment. Maturity itself does not permit inferior use; then the guardian must hand over the property, as 4:6 clarifies.
TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r3.anchor: وهذا أقوى الوجوه وليس بلوغ اليتيم أشده مما يبيح قرب ماله بغير الأحسن

TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r4.claim: Fair fulfillment of measures and weights means avoiding short measure and short weight. Since exact precision at the smallest degree is difficult, one must diligently guard against deficiency to the extent possible.
TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r4.anchor: بالعدل والوفاء من غير بخس { لا نكلف نفسا إلا وسعها } أي إلا ما يسعها

TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r5.claim: “Speak justly even about a relative” means tell the truth; making justice habitual in speech also draws one toward just action. Another interpretation specifically covers testimony and judgment concerning relatives and encompasses legal statements and rulings.
TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r5.anchor: وإنما خص القول بالعدل دون الفعل لأن من جعل عادته العدل في القول دعاه ذلك

TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r6.claim: God’s covenant can mean every obligation God imposed through command and proof, or lawful vows and agreements that people made with God; both require fulfillment.
TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r6.anchor: قيل في معنى عهد الله قولان أحدهما: أن كل ما أوجبه الله تعالى على العباد

TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r7.claim: The closing exhortation means remember God’s instructions and act on them rather than neglect them; “enjoined” gathers up the orphan-property, measures, fairness, and covenant commands.
TABRISI:6:152-153#2/r7.anchor: أي لكي تتذكروه وتأخذوا به فلا تطرحوه ولا تغفلوا عنه

TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās calls these rulings clear, un-abrogated prohibitions in all scriptures and universal commands for humanity: those who act on them enter Paradise and those who abandon them enter Hell.
TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هذه الآيات محكمات لم ينسخهن شيء من جميع الكتب

TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r5.speaker: كعب الأحبار
TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r5.claim: Kaʿb al-Aḥbār swears that these commands are the Torah’s first instruction, beginning with “Say: come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden.”
TABRISI:6:152-153#3/r5.anchor: وقال كعب الأحبار: والذي نفس كعب بيده إن هذا لأول شيء في التوراة

THALABI:v4p203/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p203/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p203/r5.claim: A guardian may approach an orphan’s property only for the orphan’s benefit and its growth.

THALABI:v4p203/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p203/r6.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v4p203/r6.claim: Mujahid says the best use of an orphan’s property is to trade with it.

THALABI:v4p203/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p203/r7.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v4p203/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak says the guardian may invest the orphan’s property but may not take any of its profit.
THALABI:v4p203/r7.anchor: وقال الضحاك: أموال يبتغي له فيه ولا يأخذ من ربحه شيئا

THALABI:v4p203/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p203/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v4p203/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd permits a poor guardian to eat reasonably from the orphan’s property but requires a wealthy guardian to abstain.
THALABI:v4p203/r8.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: وأن يأكل بالمعروف إن افتقر، وإن استغنى لم يأكل

THALABI:v4p203/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p203/r9.speaker: الشعبي
THALABI:v4p203/r9.claim: Al-Sha'bi distinguishes necessary mixing to manage the orphan’s property from mixing only to consume it; the latter should be avoided until maturity.
THALABI:v4p203/r9.anchor: وقال الشعبي: من خالط مال اليتيم حتى يفصل عليه فليخالطه

THALABI:v4p203/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p203/r10.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر
THALABI:v4p203/r10.claim: Yahya ibn Ya'mar says reaching الأشد means reaching puberty.
THALABI:v4p203/r10.anchor: وقال يحيى بن يعمر: بلوغ الحلم

THALABI:v4p203/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p203/r11.speaker: الشعبي
THALABI:v4p203/r11.claim: Al-Sha'bi says الأشد is puberty, when good and bad deeds begin to be recorded.
THALABI:v4p203/r11.anchor: وقال الشعبي: الأشد الحلم حيث يكتب له الحسنات وعليه السيئات

THALABI:v4p203/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p203/r12.speaker: أبو العالية
THALABI:v4p203/r12.claim: Abu al-Aliya says maturity comes when a person reasons well and has gathered strength.
THALABI:v4p203/r12.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: حتى يعقل ويجتمع قوته

THALABI:v4p203/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p203/r13.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v4p203/r13.claim: Al-Kalbi defines الأشد as ages eighteen to thirty.
THALABI:v4p203/r13.anchor: وقال الكلبي: الأشد ما بين ثماني عشرة إلى ثلاثين سنة

THALABI:v4p203/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p203/r14.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v4p203/r14.claim: Al-Suddi says الأشد is thirty years, followed by the separate threshold of marriageable age.
THALABI:v4p203/r14.anchor: وقال السدي: هو ثلاثون سنة ثم جاء بعدها حتى بلغوا النكاح

THALABI:v4p203/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p203/r15.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p203/r15.claim: الأشد is the plural of شد and means a person’s full strength, youth, and age; شد النهار means the day’s height or middle.
THALABI:v4p203/r15.anchor: والأشد جمع شد، مثل قد وأقد، وهو استحكام قوما لفتى وشبابه وسنه

THALABI:v4p204/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p204/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p204/r1.claim: Al-Fadl ibn Muhammad cites an Antara line using شد النهار for the height or intensity of daytime.

THALABI:v4p204/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p204/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p204/r2.claim: Reaching maturity does not permit using an orphan’s property except in the best way; once mature and prudent, the ward receives the property.
THALABI:v4p204/r2.anchor: وليس بلوغ الأشد مما يدع قرب ماله بغير الأحسن

THALABI:v4p204/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p204/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p204/r3.claim: Fulfill measure and weight fairly; the capacity limit removes hardship from both seller and buyer, requiring the seller to give the due amount and the buyer to accept the due amount.
THALABI:v4p204/r3.anchor: لا نكلف نفسا إلا وسعها أي طاقتها في إيفاء الكيل والوزن

THALABI:v4p204/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p204/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v4p204/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas warns non-Arabs that measure and weight were two causes of the destruction of earlier peoples.
THALABI:v4p204/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: إنكم معشر الأعاجم فقد وليتم أمرين بهما هلك من كان قبلكم

THALABI:v4p204/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p204/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p204/r5.claim: When speaking, be truthful in judgment and testimony even about a relative; the omitted object is the person judged or testified against.
THALABI:v4p204/r5.anchor: وإذا قلتم فاعدلوا أي فاصدقوا في الحكم والشهادة ولو كان ذا قربى

THALABI:v4p204/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p204/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v4p204/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says these clear commands were never abrogated, apply to all humanity, form the Mother of the Book, and lead their practitioners to Paradise.
THALABI:v4p204/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هذا الآيات محكمات لم ينسخهن شيء في جميع الكتب

THALABI:v4p204/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p204/r7.speaker: كعب الأحبار
THALABI:v4p204/r7.claim: Ka'b al-Ahbar says the command beginning ‘Come, I will recite what your Lord forbade’ was the first thing in the Torah.
THALABI:v4p204/r7.anchor: قال كعب الأحبار: والذي نفس كعب بيده إن هذا لأول شيء في التوراة

THALABI:v4p204/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p204/r8.speaker: الربيع بن خيثم
THALABI:v4p204/r8.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Khaytham recited these commands from a sealed sheet associated with Muhammad to his companions.
THALABI:v4p204/r8.anchor: وقال الربيع بن خيثم لأصحابه: ألا أقرأ عليكم صحيفة عليها خاتم محمد

ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n149/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n149/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n149/r1.claim: Once an orphan in one’s care comes of age, the guardian may use the property by borrowing or otherwise with the owner’s consent.
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n149/r1.anchor: the former guardian may "touch" his property, legally, by borrowing from it or otherwise utilizing it

ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n149/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n149/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n149/r2.claim: The literal “in a manner that is best” implies that any use must aim to improve the orphan’s property.
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n149/r2.anchor: which implies the intent of bettering it

ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n150/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n150/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n150/r1.claim: Full measure and weight represent equitable conduct in all dealings, not only commerce.
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n150/r1.anchor: refers metonymically to all dealings between men and not only to commercial transactions

ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n151/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n151/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n151/r1.claim: God expects people to make their best effort toward equity, not achieve mathematical exactness, which is rarely possible in human dealings.
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n151/r1.anchor: God does not expect man to behave with "mathematical" equity

ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n152/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n152/r1.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n152/r1.claim: Razi reads “when you speak” broadly as expressing an opinion on any subject, whether personally involved or not.
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n152/r1.anchor: According to Razi, the phrase "when you voice an opinion" (lit., "when you speak") applies

ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n152/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n152/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n152/r2.claim: Asad thinks the mention of near kin makes the instruction especially likely to concern giving evidence in a dispute.
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n152/r2.anchor: the subsequent reference to one's "near of kin" makes it probable that the above injunction

ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n153/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n153/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:6:151#n153/r1.claim: Asad directs readers to his explanation of the bond with God in 2:27.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p526/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p526/r4.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p526/r4.claim: A needy guardian who improves and tends the orphan’s property may take a customary amount; a wealthy one abstains, in line with 2:220’s emphasis on improving orphans’ welfare.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p526/r4.anchor: إن كنت له وصيا فأصلحت في ماله وقمت لله في ضيعته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p526/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p526/r5.speaker: الضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p526/r5.claim: The guardian should seek growth for the orphan through investment and take none of its profit.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p526/r5.anchor: هو أن يبتغي له فيه من فضل الله ولا يأخذ من ربحه شيئا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p526/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p526/r6.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p526/r6.claim: The best management of the orphan’s property is to trade with it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p526/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p526/r7.speaker: أبو إسحاق؛ السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p526/r7.claim: The best management is to preserve and grow the orphan’s assets as far as possible.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p526/r7.anchor: حفظ ماله عليه وتثميره بما يوجد السبيل إليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p528/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p528/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p528/r1.claim: Until the orphan comes of age means preserve the estate until maturity, then hand it over.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p528/r1.anchor: حتى محمولة على المعنى أي: احفظوه عليه حتى يبلغ أشده

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p528/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p528/r2.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p528/r2.claim: Ashudd is the point at which a man reaches mature judgment and knowledge.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p528/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p528/r3.speaker: أبو عبيد عن الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p528/r3.claim: Farrāʾ says ashudd would theoretically have singular shadd, though he had not heard one; a poem supplies an example of the plural.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p528/r3.anchor: الأشد واحدها شد في القياس، ولم أسمع لها بواحد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p528/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p528/r4.speaker: أبو الهيثم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p528/r4.claim: The singular is shidda, strength and toughness; the feminine ending is treated as extra when forming the plural on afʿul, like rajul/arjul.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p528/r4.anchor: واحدة الأشد: شدة، كما أن واحدة الأنعم: نعمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p528/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p528/r5.speaker: ابن الأنباري؛ جماعة من البصريين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p528/r5.claim: Some linguists treat ashudd as a singular without a singular form; some Basrans give its singular as shudd with a ḍamma.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p528/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p528/r6.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p528/r6.claim: The span of ashudd begins at adult maturity and ends at forty, with the endpoints fixed but the interval unspecified; 46:15 also links ashudd and forty.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p528/r6.anchor: وبلوغ الأشد يكون من وقت بلوغ الإنسان مبلغ الرجال وإدراكه إلى أربعين سنة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p528/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p528/r7.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر؛ السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p528/r7.claim: In this verse, reaching ashudd is interpreted as puberty, specifically a wet dream.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p528/r7.anchor: وفسر بلوغ الأشد في هذه الآية بالاحتلام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p528/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p528/r8.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p528/r8.claim: The orphan must be both physically mature and sound in judgment before receiving his money; the author refers back to the discussion at the start of Sūrat al-Nisāʾ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p528/r8.anchor: وبلوغ أشده أن يونس منه الرشد مع أن يكون بالغا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p531/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p531/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p531/r1.claim: Wafāʾ means completion; fulfilling the measure means giving its full amount without short measure.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p531/r1.anchor: وأوفى الكيل، أي: أتمه ولم ينقص منه شيئا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p531/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p531/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p531/r2.claim: Al-mīzān means weighing with the scale, not completing the scale itself; the wording omits the understood noun “weight,” just as “measure” omits “measuring vessel.”

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p531/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p531/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p531/r3.claim: Qisṭ means justice, with neither shortchanging nor excess.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p531/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p531/r4.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p531/r4.claim: God has made lawful and unlawful dealings known; sellers should give buyers the full measure they themselves want when purchasing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p531/r4.anchor: فكما تحب أن يوفيك من تشتري منه، فأوف من تبيع منه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p531/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p531/r5.speaker: أصحاب المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p531/r5.claim: The seller must give the exact due without extra burden, and the buyer must accept the exact due without demanding a shortfall; neither is required to do what exceeds capacity.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p531/r5.anchor: أمر الله تعالى المعطي بإيفاء ذي الحق حقه الذي هو له من غير زيادة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p532/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p532/r1.speaker: ابن عباس؛ الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p532/r1.claim: When speaking or testifying, tell the truth even if the person concerned is a child, relative, or someone beloved; the omitted party may be either witness beneficiary or accused, as al-Zajjāj explains, paralleling 5:106.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p532/r1.anchor: إذا شهدتم أو تكلمتم فقولوا الحق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p532/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p532/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p532/r2.claim: The covenant with God’s name is explained by the discussion of keeping covenants at 2:40.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p532/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p532/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p532/r3.claim: The closing command gathers orphan-property care, just measures, capacity, truth even about relatives, and keeping promises, so people remember and act on them; the promise reward is cited at 48:10.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p532/r3.anchor: ذلك الذي تقدم من ذكر مال اليتيم، وأن لا يقرب إلا بالتي هي أحسن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p532/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p532/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p532/r4.claim: Tadhakkur is repeated remembering; tadhakkarūn is contracted from tatadhakkarūn by assimilation of neighboring consonants.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p532/r4.anchor: وتذكر مطاوع ذكر (¬4) تقول: ذكرته فتذكر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p532/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p532/r5.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p532/r5.claim: They read tadhakkarūn with a light dhāl, deleting a consonant rather than assimilating it; the author says deletion could be preferable as lighter while meaning remains clear.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:149-152/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:149-152/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:149-152/r4.claim: Protect orphans’ assets by improving and growing them; a needy guardian may take a customary amount, and the property is guarded until puberty.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:149-152/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:149-152/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:149-152/r5.claim: Give full measure and fair weight without shortchanging or excess; requiring extra from the giver or too little from the recipient would exceed what each can bear.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:149-152/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:149-152/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:149-152/r6.claim: When speaking or testifying, state the truth even when it concerns a close relative.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:149-152/r6.anchor: إذا شهدتم أو تكلمتم فقولوا الحق

ELMALILI:6:152-153/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r1.claim: Do not approach an orphan's property except through the best guardianship, protecting and growing it and delivering it when the orphan reaches maturity.
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r1.anchor: hıfz u tenmiye ve zamanında teslim gibi- en güzel suretle tekarrub -mümkin olan en güzel velâyet ve vesâyet

ELMALILI:6:152-153/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r2.claim: Fulfill measure and weight with fairness: use neither deficient nor excessive measures and do not cheat when measuring or weighing.
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r2.anchor: Hem noksan veya fazla ölçü kullanmayınız, hem de ölçer ve tartarken eksik veya fazla yapmayınız

ELMALILI:6:152-153/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r3.claim: The measure rule protects others' rights generally, so transgressing another person's rights is forbidden even when no orphan property is involved.
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r3.anchor: yetim malı olmasa bile hukūk-ı gayra tecavüz de haramdır

ELMALILI:6:152-153/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r4.claim: Justice can be difficult, but people are required to observe it within their capacity and are excused for what exceeds it.
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r4.anchor: adl ü tesviye haddizâtında zor bir şey ise de buna da vüs‘ünüz kadar riayetle mükellefsiniz

ELMALILI:6:152-153/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r5.claim: Whenever people speak in judgment, testimony, government, or any other matter, they must state what is true and right.
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r5.anchor: gerek hükûmet ve gerek şehadet ve gerek herhangi bir hususta bir söz söylediğiniz vakit hakkını, doğrusunu söyleyiniz

ELMALILI:6:152-153/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r6.claim: Truthful speech is required even when the person helped or harmed by one's words is a relative; favoritism is forbidden.
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r6.anchor: velevse leh veya aleyhinde söyleyeceğiniz kimse akrabanızdan olsun yine doğru söyleyiniz, tarafdarlık etmeyiniz

ELMALILI:6:152-153/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r7.claim: God's covenants include His commands and prohibitions and valid pledges people make to God or in God's name, including vows, oaths, and contracts.
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r7.anchor: gerek Allah’ın size teklif etmiş olduğu ahidleri, emirleri, nehiyleri ve gerek sizin Allah’a veya Allah nâmına diğerlerine verdiğiniz ahidleri

ELMALILI:6:152-153/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r8.claim: Every valid commitment must be fulfilled; breaking a covenant is forbidden.
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r8.anchor: nezirleri, yeminleri, akidleri sahih olan her nevi ta‘ahhüdâtı tamamen yerine getiriniz. Nakz-ı ahd de haramdır

ELMALILI:6:152-153/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r9.claim: The command's obligation and prohibition of its opposite span every religious command, prohibition, and covenant across faith and practice.
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r9.anchor: bu emirden müstefâd olan vücub ve zıddının hurmeti iman ve amel hudûdunun şâmil olduğu her nevi evâmir ü nevâhî ile bütün uhûda mütenâvildir

ELMALILI:6:152-153/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r10.claim: The broad covenant command includes the ban on manifest and hidden sin and the worship, lawful, unlawful, and other rulings already discussed.
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r10.anchor: buraya kadar sebk eden ibâdât, hıll u hurmet vesâire ahkâmı hep burada dâhildir

ELMALILI:6:152-153/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r11.claim: Remembering the commands means keeping them in mind, considering their deeper content, and acting accordingly.
ELMALILI:6:152-153/r11.anchor: Bunları iyice hatırınızda tutasınız ve zımnındaki derin muhteveyâtını düşünesiniz de mûcebiyle amel eyleyesiniz

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r1.claim: After criticizing baseless polytheist rules, these verses set out nine principal divine commands on monotheism and morality, then command following God's straight path as the encompassing duty; the invitation frames these as the sole correct and obligatory way.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r1.anchor: bu âyetlerde asıl benimsenmesi gereken başlıca ilâhî kurallar ve hükümler yer almakta

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r14.claim: Although everyone's property is inviolable, an orphan's assets merit special care because vulnerability exposes them to abuse; total neglect can erode the assets, so proper care is permitted and implicitly encouraged as virtuous.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r14.anchor: “en iyi ve en güzel” (ahsen) kaydından anlaşıldığı kadarıyla ilgilenmek zımnen teşvik edilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r15.claim: Trade often brings injustice in measures and weights; since perfect fairness may exceed human capacity, the following limit of capacity indicates inadvertent errors are not blameworthy, and Razi reads the wording as requiring both seller and buyer to uphold fairness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r15.anchor: burada geçen ifa kavramı tam olarak ölçüp tartmayı ifade etmekle birlikte ayrıca bir de kıst (adalet) kelimesinin geçmesinden anlaşılıyor ki

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r16.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r16.claim: Justice in speech includes every verbal relation, from reporting and contracts to advice and criticism, and excludes speech intended to wrong, hurt, or insult; the clause about close relatives warns against bias from affection or pity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r16.anchor: âyetteki “yakınlarınız bile olsa” kaydıyla bu hususta özellikle uyarıda bulunulmuştur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r17.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r17.claim: God's covenant means all duties He imposes; Muslims have pledged to follow His rules, and the command also covers keeping lawful promises to people.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:151/r17.anchor: Allah’ın ahdinden maksat, O’nun kullarına yüklediği her türlü vazifelerdir

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p129.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p129.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p129.claim: The basic teachings of Abraham's religion call Quraysh to the straight path; Moses' law likewise guides its adherents to that path.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p129.anchor: the Quraysh too are invited to this straight path. They must not deviate from them and wander in misguidance.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p147.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p147.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p147.claim: These verses detail Abraham's religion and expose the Quraysh's neglect of its duties to God and creatures while claiming adherence through invented food taboos; their first violation is polytheism.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p147.anchor: These verses state the real religion of Abraham (sws) in detail.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p147.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p147.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p147.claim: The passage states some duties positively and others negatively; as in 17:22–38, each form implies its opposite, such as monotheism from the ban on polytheism and kind treatment from the duty to honor parents.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p147.anchor: Exactly the same style has been adopted in these directives in verses 22-38 of Sūrah Banī Isrā’īl.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.claim: Orphan wealth must be approached only for the orphan's benefit, managed and increased, then returned at maturity in the presence of witnesses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.anchor: The only proper way to go near their wealth is to manage it and further enhance it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.claim: The positive command to give full measure implies its opposite is forbidden; 83:1–3 condemns short measure.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p150.anchor: Woe be to those who weigh and measure less!

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p151.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p151.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p151.claim: The universe rests on justice; honest measure supports a just economy, while dishonest dealings prevent development, spread disorder, and bring a nation's destruction under God's established practice.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p151.anchor: Nations which are dishonest in their dealings have never developed in this world nor is their any chance for them to do so.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p151.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p151.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p151.claim: God's commands fit human capacity and inadvertent mistakes are overlooked; the verse also rejects both excessive caution and the claim that individuals may set their own limit of obedience.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p151.anchor: Nothing among them are beyond their capacity and capability. Secondly, everyone must follow these directives with full honesty and veracity

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p151.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p151.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p151.claim: Speaking truth even about relatives is general, but here specifically requires truthful testimony and decisions regardless of kinship; 17:36 also prohibits claiming what one does not know.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p151.anchor: no evidence borne and no decision given by people should be against the truth even if the matter relates to their relatives.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p151.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p151.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p151.claim: Fulfilling God's promise includes His covenants and people's promises to one another for noble causes; every promise within God's limits makes its keeper accountable to God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p151.anchor: This includes promises which God has taken from people as well as those which they make with one another for any noble cause.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.claim: The sequence moves from reflection that frees one from blind following, to recalling truths of human nature, then to taqwā; Sharīʿah's fundamentals emerge from human nature when people heed God's reminder.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.anchor: The sharī‘ah is a treasury that has been extracted from our nature and has been consigned to us

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.claim: Just as wholesome purity distinguishes lawful food, justice, goodness, and good conventions distinguish commanded conduct from rebellion, lewdness, and vice in Abraham's and Islam's religions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p152.anchor: all things that are enjoined stem from justice, goodness and good conventions and all things that are forbidden stem from rebelliousness, lewdness and vice.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p424/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p424/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p424/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr geminate the listed forms of ذكر throughout, including يذكرون, تذكرون, يذكر الإنسان, أن يذكر, and ليذكروا.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p424/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو: يذكرون*، وتذكرون*، ويذكر الإنسان [مريم/ 67]

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p424/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p424/r2.speaker: نافع وعاصم وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p424/r2.claim: Nafi, Asim through Abu Bakr, and Ibn Amir generally geminate these forms but lighten the reading أولا يذكر الإنسان; Hafs and another Asim transmission lighten تذكرون throughout.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p424/r2.anchor: وقرأ نافع وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر وابن عامر: كل ذلك بالتشديد إلا قوله: أولا يذكر الإنسان

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p424/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p424/r3.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p424/r3.claim: Hamza and Kisai geminate yadhakkarun when it begins with yāʾ and lighten tadhakkarun with tāʾ; at 25:62 Hamza lightens while Kisai geminates, and both lighten the cited liyadhakkaru forms.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p424/r3.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي: يذكرون* مشددا إذا كان بالياء، وتذكرون مخففا إذا كان بالتاء.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p424/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p424/r4.speaker: نافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p424/r4.claim: All readers lighten the dhāl in وما يذكرون at 74:56; Nafi reads its verb with tāʾ, while the others use yāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p424/r4.anchor: واتفقوا على تخفيف ذال قوله : وما يذكرون ورفع الكاف في المدثر [56].

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p424/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p424/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p424/r5.claim: Sibawayh says ذكر takes one object, but doubling its middle radical gives it two; Form V تذكر is the corresponding reflexive or responsive form, as in the cited verse and poetry.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p424/r5.anchor: فإذا ضاعفت العين تعدى إلى مفعولين

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p426/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p426/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p426/r1.claim: The verbal noun appears as ادكار and ذكرى; ذِكر has the plural الذكر, and a dāl pronunciation occurs through the word's frequent assimilation, though dhāl is the regular form.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p426/r1.anchor: وجاء المصدر على ذكرى بألف التأنيث، كما جاء على فعلى

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p426/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p426/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p426/r2.claim: Form VIII ادكر may be transitive, like other verbs that gain transitivity through the added form; the cited Qur'anic wording and poetry support this usage.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p426/r2.anchor: ويجوز في القياس أن يكون ادكرت متعديا مثل: شويته، واشتويته،

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p426/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p426/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p426/r3.claim: Remembering the community's former weakness in 8:26, as in 7:86, means comparing past hardship with present favor so they will give thanks.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p426/r3.anchor: فأما قوله: واذكروا إذ أنتم قليل مستضعفون في الأرض [الأنفال/ 26]، فمن الذكر الذي يكون عن النسيان

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p426/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p426/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p426/r4.claim: ذلكم وصاكم recalls the duties just listed: protect the orphan's property, measure fairly within capacity, speak and judge justly even for kin, and fulfill God's covenant.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p426/r4.anchor: ذلك الذي تقدم ذكره في ذكر مال اليتيم، وأن لا يقرب إلا بالتي هي أحسن

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p426/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p426/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p426/r5.claim: The capacity limit qualifies those obligations, and fulfilling the covenant carries the reward promised in 48:10.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p426/r5.anchor: ولذلك أتبع بقوله: لا نكلف نفسا إلا وسعها [الأنعام/ 152]، والقول بالقسط والحق

IBNMUJAHID:v1p272/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p272/r1.speaker: نافع، عاصم عن أبي بكر، ابن عامر، حفص، حمزة، الكسائي، أبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p272/r1.claim: The readers vary in forms of تذكرون: several traditions use doubling, while Ali ibn Nasr and Hafs report lightening throughout; Hamza and al-Kisai distinguish yāʾ forms from tāʾ forms, with further exceptions in al-Furqan and al-Isra.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p272/r1.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائى ﴿ يذكرون ﴾ مشددا إذا كان بالياء

QIRAAT-ER:6:152:45#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:6:152:45#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:6:152:45#1/r1.claim: Assimilating tāʾ into dhāl simplifies tatadhakkarūna to tadhdhakkarūna without changing meaning; the heavier cluster may echo active remembrance.
QIRAAT-ER:6:152:45#1/r1.anchor: Full assimilation of tāʾ into dhāl (tadhdhakkarūna from tatadhakkarūna) — phonological simplification

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r7.claim: The prohibition on approaching orphan property covers every kind of handling and blocks means to misuse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r7.anchor: هذا نهي عن القرب الذي يعم جميع وجوه التصرف، وفيه سد الذريعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r8.claim: It singles out the orphan because guardians are especially tempted by the wealth and the child has little power to protect it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r8.anchor: ونص على اليتيم لأن الطمع فيه أكثر لضعفه وقلة مراعاته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس وابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r9.claim: They explain best treatment as improving the property and taking a customary amount only when the guardian needs it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r9.anchor: هو أن يعمل له عملا مصلحا فيأكل منه بالمعروف وقت الحاجة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r10.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r10.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the guardian should preserve and increase the orphan's wealth.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r11.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r11.claim: Al-Dahhak says to retain profits by trading the property and take nothing from it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r11.anchor: وقال الضحاك: حفظ ربحه بالتجارة ولا يأخذ منه شيئا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r12.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r12.claim: Mujahid permits trade; a wealthy guardian should take no expense or fee, while a needy guardian may use a reasonable amount from the trading profit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r12.anchor: فمن كان من الناظرين له مال يعيش به فالأحسن إذ أثمر مال اليتيم أن لا يأخذ منه نفقة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r13.speaker: المروزي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r13.claim: One view permits using the orphan's animals and employing enslaved women so guardians need not mix households.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r13.anchor: وقيل: الانتفاع بدوابه واستخدام جواريه لئلا يخرج الأولياء بالمخالطة ذكره المروزي.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r14.claim: A view allowing only a loan from the orphan is rejected as inconsistent with what is best for the child.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p687#2/r14.anchor: وقيل: لا يأكل منه إلا قرضا وهذا بعيد وأي أحسنية في هذا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r1.claim: The endpoint is semantic rather than syntactic: guard the orphan's wealth until maturity, then hand it over.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r1.anchor: هذه غاية من حيث المعنى لا من حيث هذا التركيب اللفظي، ومعناه احفظوا على اليتيم ماله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r2.speaker: الشعبي وزيد بن أسلم ويحيى بن يعمر وربيعة ومالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r2.claim: They define the orphan's reaching maturity as puberty; al-Shaʿbi, Rabiʿa, Malik, and Abu Hanifa are also reported to require puberty without established misconduct.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r2.anchor: وبلوغ الأشد هنا لليتيم هو بلوغ الحلم قاله الشعبي وزيد بن أسلم ويحيى بن يعمر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas gives adulthood as ages eighteen to thirty, and elsewhere thirty-three.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r3.anchor: فعن ابن عباس ما بين ثماني عشرة إلى ثلاثين وعنه ثلاث وثلاثون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r4.speaker: ابن جبير ومقاتل والسدي والثوري وعكرمة وعائشة وأبو العالية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r4.claim: Reported age definitions range from eighteen, twenty-five, thirty, thirty-four, or forty; Abu al-ʿAliya instead describes maturity as sound judgment and full strength, and other reports say fifteen to thirty or sixty.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r4.anchor: وعن ابن جبير ومقاتل ثماني عشرة وعن السدي ثلاثون وعن الثوري أربع وثلاثون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r5.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r5.claim: Ibn al-Anbari prefers treating ashudd as a singular with no plural form, but Abu Hayyan rejects this because afʿal is not used as a singular noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r5.anchor: اختار ابن الأنباري في آخرين الأخير وليس بمختار لفقدان أفعل في المفردات وضعا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r6.claim: Ashudd has five proposed morphological analyses: plural of shidda, plural of shadd, a plural without a matching singular, or a singular without a plural, among them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r6.anchor: وأشد جمع شدة أو شد أو شد أو جمع لا واحد له من لفظه أو مفرد لا جمع له أقوال خمسة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r7.claim: The word derives from strength and firmness; another etymology connects it to rising, as in Antar's description of the day rising.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r7.anchor: وأشد مشتق من الشدة وهي القوة والجلادة. وقيل: أصله الارتفاع من شد النهار إذا ارتفع.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r8.speaker: عنترة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r8.claim: Antar's line uses shadda al-nahār to witness the sense of the sun's height.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r8.anchor: عهدي به شد النهار كأنما ... خضب اللبان ورأسه بالعظلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r9.claim: Qist means fairness and exact balance; another view recommends slight over-measure to ensure the duty is certainly fulfilled, supported by a report to add weight.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r9.anchor: أي بالعدل والتسوية. وقيل: القسط هنا أدنى زيادة ليخرج بها عن العهدة بيقين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r10.speaker: الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r10.claim: Al-Tabari says the obligation in measure is the amount humanly possible; perfect accuracy beyond capacity is not required.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r10.anchor: فالواجب في إيفاء الكيل والميزان هو القدر الممكن وأما التحقيق فغير واجب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r11.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the clause may mean duties must stay within human capacity rather than demanding perfect precision in every transaction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p688/r11.anchor: يقتضي أن هذه الأوامر إنما هي فيما يقع تحت قدرة البشر من التحفظ والتحرز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r1.claim: Fair speech means neither adding nor withholding when a relative is concerned; the speaker's own self, parents, and kin are included.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r1.anchor: أي ولو كان المقول له أو عليه ذا قرابة للقائل فلا ينبغي أن يزيد ولا ينقص

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r2.claim: The command covers matters known only by speech, including judgments, testimony, admonition, and mediation; limiting it to a particular category lacks evidence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r2.anchor: وعنى بالقول هنا ما لا يطلع عليه إلا بالقول من أمر وحكم وشهادة زجر ووساطة بين الناس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r3.claim: The genitive in God's covenant can mean a covenant God made with people or one people made with God; it may also refer to covenants between people, whose keeping God commands.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r3.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون مضافا إلى الفاعل أي بما عهدكم الله عليه أوفوا وأن يكون مضافا إلى المفعول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r4.speaker: الماتريدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r4.claim: Al-Maturidi interprets God's covenant as His commands and prohibitions regarding lawful and unlawful things.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r4.anchor: قال الماتريدي: أمره ونهيه في التحليل والتحريم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r5.speaker: التبريزي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r5.claim: Al-Tabrizi takes the covenant as the primordial covenant on the Day of the Covenant.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r6.speaker: ابن الجوزي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r6.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi says the wording includes God's instructions and what people obligate themselves to, such as vows.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r6.anchor: يشمل ما عهده إلى الخلق وأوصاهم به وعلى ما أوجبه الإنسان على نفسه من نذر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r7.claim: The first five duties are clear and end with understanding; the remaining four are subtle and require effortful reflection, so they end with remembrance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r7.anchor: ولما كانت الخمسة المذكورة قبل هذا من الأمور الظاهرة الجلية وجب تعلقها وتفهمها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r8.speaker: حفص والأخوان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r8.claim: Hafs and the two Kufan readers lighten the dhāl by dropping one tā from tatadhakkarūn; they differ over which tā is deleted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r8.anchor: حيث وقع بتخفيف الذال حذفت التاء إذ أصله تتذكرون، وفي المحذوف خلاف أهي تاء المضارعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r9.speaker: باقي السبعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r9.claim: The other canonical readers pronounce the word with a doubled dhāl, assimilating the tāʾ of the form into it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p689/r9.anchor: بتشديده أدغم تاء تفعل في الذال

ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r1.claim: Do not approach an orphan's wealth in any way except by the best practice for his benefit, such as protecting and investing it; the alternative that the guardian must personally embody the best quality is called remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r1.anchor: إلا بالتي هي أحسن ( أي بالفعلة التي هي أحسن ما يفعل بماله كحفظه وتثميره

ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r2.claim: The audience is guardians and trustees; 'until he reaches maturity' ends the implied duty to preserve the property, after which it must be handed to the orphan as in 4:6.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r2.anchor: والخطاب للأولياء والأوصياء لقوله تعالى : ( حتى يبلغ أشده ( فإنه غاية لما يفهم من الاستثناء لا للنهي

ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r3.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r3.claim: Al-Farra says ashudd is a plural with no singular; some Basrans treat it as singular, while other grammarians derive it from forms meaning severity or strength.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r3.anchor: والأشد على ما قاله الفراء جمع لا واحد له وقال بعض البصريين : هو مفرد كأنك

ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r4.speaker: عنترة
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r4.claim: Antara's verse uses 'shadd al-nahar' for the height of the day, one proposed derivation of ashudd.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r4.anchor: ومنه قول عنترة : عهدي به شد النهار كأنما خضب ورأسه بالعظلم

ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r5.speaker: الشعبي وجماعة
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r5.claim: Al-Shaʿbi and a group define reaching ashudd as puberty; another opinion sets it at eighteen, while al-Suddi says thirty.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r5.anchor: والمراد ببلوغ الأشد عند الشعبي وجماعة بلوغ الحلم وقيل : أن يبلغ ثماني عشرة سنة وقال السدي : أن يبلغ ثلاثين

ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r6.speaker: some exegetes
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r6.claim: Some say the maturity ruling is abrogated by the instruction to test orphans until they reach marriage and then give them their assets.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r6.anchor: إلا أن الآية منسوخة بقوله تعالى : ( حتى إذا بلغوا النكاح )

ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r7.claim: The source refers readers to its earlier detailed treatment of the disputed age for handing over an orphan's property.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r7.anchor: وقد تقدم الخلاف في زمن دفع مال اليتيم إليه وأشبعنا الكلام في تحقيق الحق في ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r8.claim: Fulfill the measured amount and the weight; kayl may mean the measured commodity, and an omitted noun may be supplied with each verbal noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r8.anchor: أي أتموا ( الكيل ( أي المكيل فهو مصدر بمعنى اسم المفعول والميزان ( كذلك كما قال أبو البقاء

ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r9.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r9.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows 'with fairness' to describe the subject as dealing justly or the object as complete measure.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r9.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء : يجوز أن يكون حالا من المفعول أي تاما

ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r10.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r10.claim: Al-Razi explains that sellers must give the entitled party the full due without shortchanging, while buyers must take their due without demanding an excess.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r10.anchor: أمر الله تعالى المعطي بإيفاء ذي الحق حقه من غير نقصان وأمر صاحب الحق بأخذ حقه من غير طلب الزيادة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r11.claim: God does not burden anyone beyond capacity; following exact measure can be difficult when frequently required, so the command is limited to what is feasible and excess is excused.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r11.anchor: للترخيص فيما خرج عن الطاقة لما أن في مراعاة ذلك كما هو حرجا مع كثرة وقوعه

ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r12.claim: The preceding obligations are feasible rather than burdensome; God does not impose the impossible.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r12.anchor: من التكليفات ليقبلوا عليها كأنه قيل : جميع ما كلفناكم به ممكن غير شاق ونحن لا نكلف ما لا يطاق

ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r13.claim: When speaking in judgment or testimony, people must be just and truthful even when a relative is involved.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r13.anchor: فاعدلوا ( فيه وقولوا الحق ( ولو كان ( المقول له أو عليه ( ذا قربى

ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r14.claim: Fulfill whatever covenant was made, especially those listed here and promises to God such as oaths and vows; the fronted phrase emphasizes the covenant with God.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r14.anchor: أي ما عهد اليكم من الامور المعدودة أو أي عهد كان فيدخل فيه ما ذكر دخولا أوليا

ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r15.claim: The closing sentence says God emphatically enjoined these duties so people will remember them.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p55#2/r15.anchor: ذلكم ( أي ما فصل من التكاليف الجليلة ( وصاكم به ( أمركم به أمرا مؤكذا ( لعلكم تذكرون

ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r1.speaker: حمرة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r1.claim: Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Hafs from Asim read tadhakkarun with a light dhāl; the other readers geminate it throughout the Qur'an, with the same meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r1.anchor: وقرأ حمرة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم تذكرون بتخفيف الذال والباقون بالتشديد في كل القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r2.speaker: القطب الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r2.claim: Al-Qutb al-Razi says the first verse ends with 'reason' because people committed its sins heedlessly, while the second ends with 'remember' because they already practiced and took pride in its duties but might forget them.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r2.anchor: لأن القوم كانوا مستمرين على الشرك وقتل الأولاد وقربان الزنا وقتل النفس المحرمة بغير حق غير مستنكفين ولا عاقلين قبحها

ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r3.speaker: القطب الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r3.claim: Asked why honoring parents, already practiced, is in the first set, al-Razi answers that parents' blessing follows God's and their care in childhood makes ingratitude especially serious.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r3.anchor: أعظم النعم على الإنسان نعمة الله تعالى ويتلوها نعمة الوالدين لأنهما المؤثران في الظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r4.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r4.claim: Al-Razi instead says the first five duties are obvious and call for rational recognition, while the four later duties are subtle and require thought to find the balanced course.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r4.anchor: التكاليف الخمسة المذكورة في الآية الأولى ظاهرة جلية فوجب تعقلها وتفهمها

ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r5.claim: Al-Alusi suggests that the first set is mostly prohibitions, whose restraint suits the idea of reason holding one back, whereas the later commands need emphasis so they persist in memory.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p56/r5.anchor: إن أكثر التكليفات الأول أدى بصيغة النهي وهو في معنى المنع والمرء حريص على ما منع

ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r3.claim: A hasan report from Ibn Masud says whoever wishes to see the Prophet's testament bearing his seal should recite the verses beginning 'Say: come, I will recite' through 'that you may be mindful.'
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r3.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه قال : من سره أن ينظر إلى وصية محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام بخاتمه

ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r4.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r4.claim: Ubadah reports that the Prophet sought a pledge on these three verses: fulfillment earns God's reward; a shortcoming punished in this life is expiated, while a deferred matter is left to God's choice to punish or pardon.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r4.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أيكم يبايعني على هؤلاء الآيات الثلاث ثم تلاهن إلى آخرهن

ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says these decisive verses have never been abrogated in any scripture, are forbidden to all humanity, are the Mother of the Book, and lead their practitioners to Paradise and abandoners to the Fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p57/r6.anchor: هذه آيات محكمات لم ينسخهن شيء من جميع الكتب وهن محرمات على بني آدم كلهم وهن أم الكتاب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203#2/r1.claim: Approach orphan property only to benefit and grow it; Mujahid says trade with it, while al-Dahhak says seek its profit without taking any of that profit.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203#2/r1.anchor: {ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم إلا بالتي هي أحسن} يعني: بما فيه صلاحه وتثميره.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203#2/r2.speaker: الشعبي ومالك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203#2/r2.claim: They define reaching full strength as puberty, when good and bad deeds begin to be recorded.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203#2/r2.anchor: قال الشعبي ومالك: الأشد: الحلم، حتى يكتب له الحسنات

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203#2/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203#2/r3.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya says full strength means understanding and the body's powers coming together.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو العالية: حتى يعقل وتجتمع قوته.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203#2/r4.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203#2/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi defines full strength as ages eighteen through thirty; other reports extend it to forty or sixty, while al-Dahhak says twenty, al-Suddi thirty, and Mujahid thirty-three.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203#2/r4.anchor: وقال الكلبي: الأشد ما بين الثمانية عشر سنة إلى ثلاثين سنة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203#2/r5.claim: Ashudd is a plural of strength; it denotes the full vigor of youth and age, with a comparison to the sun's height at midday.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203#2/r5.anchor: والأشد جمع شد، مثل قد وأقد، وهو استحكام قوة شبابه وسنه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203#2/r6.claim: Another view says full strength is reaching sound judgment after puberty; then the verse requires protecting the orphan's wealth until that point and delivering it if he is prudent.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p203#2/r6.anchor: وقيل بلوغ الأشد أن يؤنس رشده بعد البلوغ. وتقدير الآية:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204/r1.claim: Measure and weigh fairly within people's capacity: the seller need not give more than due, and the rights-holder need not accept less; each must do what is manageable without hardship.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204/r1.anchor: {وأوفوا الكيل والميزان بالقسط} بالعدل، {لا نكلف نفسا إلا وسعها} أي: طاقتها في إيفاء الكيل والميزان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204/r2.claim: When speaking, judge and testify truthfully even against a relative; fulfill God's covenant, so that you may take heed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204/r2.anchor: {وإذا قلتم فاعدلوا} فاصدقوا في الحكم والشهادة، {ولو كان ذا قربى}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204/r3.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204/r3.claim: They read tadhakkarūn with a light dhal throughout the Qur'an; other readers geminate it.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says these commands are fixed in all scriptures, never abrogated, prohibited to all humanity, and are the Mother of the Book; whoever follows them enters Paradise and whoever abandons them enters Hell.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p204/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هذه الآيات محكمات في جميع الكتب، لم ينسخهن شيء

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:152/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:152/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:152/r1.claim: Approach an orphan's property only by the best conduct, such as preserving and growing it; ashudd means adulthood, perhaps a plural or singular.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:152/r1.anchor: أي بالفعلة التي هي أحسن ما يفعل بماله كحفظه وتثميره. { حتى يبلغ أشده } حتى يصير بالغا

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:152/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:152/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:152/r2.claim: Give full measure and weight fairly; because fulfillment may be difficult, require only what each person can manage and forgive the rest.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:152/r2.anchor: إلا ما يسعها ولا يعسر عليها، وذكره عقيب الأمر معناه أن إيفاء الحق عسر عليكم

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:152/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:152/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:152/r3.claim: Speak equitably in judgments even when a relative is involved; God's covenant is to maintain justice and carry out religious law.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:152/r3.anchor: في حكومة ونحوها. { فاعدلوا } فيه. { ولو كان ذا قربى } ولو كان المقول له أو عليه من ذوي قرابتكم

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:152/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:152/r4.speaker: حمزة وحفص والكسائي
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:152/r4.claim: Hamza, Hafs, and al-Kisai read tadhakkarūn with a light dhāl when the word has tāʾ; the others double it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:152/r4.anchor: وقرأ حمزة وحفص والكسائي { تذكرون } بتخفيف الذال حيث وقع إذا كان بالتاء

BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r1.claim: Because property sustains life, the verse begins its next set of rules with wealth and singles out the vulnerable orphan’s property; even approaching it is prohibited except to improve and grow it.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r1.anchor: ولما كان أعظمها خطرا وحرمة مال اليتيم لضعفه وقلة ناصره

BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r2.claim: Guardians may manage the orphan’s property only in the best way, such as developing and investing it, until the child reaches customary maturity and discernment.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r2.anchor: وهو سن يبلغ به أوان حصول عقله عادة وعقل يظهر به رشده

BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r3.claim: Fair measure means full, equitable delivery without excess or shortfall; the qualification removes any implication that merely coming close is enough.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r3.anchor: أي إيفاء كائنا به من غير إفراط ولا تفريط

BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
