BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r4.claim: Exact equality is often unattainable, so people owe sincere effort within their ability; anything beyond capacity is excused.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r4.anchor: أشار إلى أنه ليس على المكلف المبني أمره على العجز للضعف إلا الجهد

BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r5.claim: When speaking in testimony, judgment, mediation, or any other matter, people must be just even about relatives, resisting affection, fear, or hopes of support.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r5.anchor: أي في شهادة أو في حكم أو توفيق بين اثنين أو غير ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r6.claim: God’s covenant covers everything a person owes or is owed; the closing charge emphasizes remembering justice by judging for others as one would judge for oneself.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p742/r6.anchor: وهذا يشمل كل ما على الإنسان وله , فإن الله لم يهمل شيئا بغير تقدم فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p743/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p743/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p743/r1.claim: The rulings are distributed across three verses, each ending with “He has charged you,” strengthening the instruction and inviting acceptance.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p743/r1.anchor: وفصل ما هنا من الأحكام في ثلاث آيات , وختم كل آية لذلك بالوصية

BIQAI-FULL:v2p743/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p743/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p743/r2.claim: The closing appeals progress from reason to remembrance to taqwa: reason calls for reflection, which leads to precaution against straying and ruin.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p743/r2.anchor: لأنه إذا كان العقل دعا إلى التذكير فحمل على التقوى

DURR-FULL:v3p244/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r3.claim: Al-An‘am was revealed in Mecca as a whole except these three verses, which were revealed in Medina.
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: سورة الأنعام نزلت بمكة جملة واحدة فهي مكية إلا ثلاث آيات

DURR-FULL:v3p244/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r8.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r8.claim: Al-An‘am descended all at once with ranks of angels stretching from the lowest heaven to earth; it was Meccan except 6:151–153.
DURR-FULL:v3p244/r8.anchor:
عن شهر بن
حوشب قال: نزلت الأنعام جملة واحدة معها رجز من الملائكة

DURR-FULL:v3p380/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r4.claim: The Prophet’s sealed testament is found in the three concluding commandments of al-An‘am.
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r4.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: من سره أن ينظر إلى وصية محمد التي عليها خاتما

DURR-FULL:v3p380/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r5.claim: The Prophet sought a pledge to uphold these three verses: fulfillment earns reward, while shortcoming may be punished in life or left to God’s will in the afterlife.
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r5.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أيكم يبايعني على هؤلاء الآيات الثلاث

DURR-FULL:v3p380/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r6.speaker: الربيع بن خثيم
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r6.claim: When asked for a written sheet bearing the Prophet’s seal, al-Rabi‘ recited these concluding verses from al-An‘am.
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r6.anchor: قال الربيع بن خيثم: أيسرك أن تلقى صحيفة من محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بخاتم

DURR-FULL:v3p380/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r7.speaker: كعب
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r7.claim: Ka‘b says the first ten revealed verses of the Torah are these ten commandments at the end of al-An‘am.
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r7.anchor: عن كعب قال: أول ما نزل من التوراة عشر آيات

DURR-FULL:v3p380/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r8.speaker: كعب
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r8.claim: Ka‘b swears that the first verse in the Torah is the opening of these commandments from al-An‘am.
DURR-FULL:v3p380/r8.anchor: عن عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن عدي بن الخيار قال: سمع كعب رجلا يقرأ

DURR-FULL:v3p382/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p382/r1.speaker: الربيع بن خثيم
DURR-FULL:v3p382/r1.claim: Asked for advice, al-Rabi‘ wrote down the three commandments at the end of al-An‘am and told the questioner to adhere to them.
DURR-FULL:v3p382/r1.anchor: عن مزاحم بن زفر قال: قال رجل للربيع بن خيثم: أوصني

DURR-FULL:v3p382/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p382/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p382/r2.claim: At Mina, the Prophet invited an Arab tribe to affirm God’s oneness, recognize his messengership, and shelter and defend him; he recited these commandments, then 16:90. Mafruq praised their noble morals and Hani‘ approved his words.
DURR-FULL:v3p382/r2.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: ادعوكم إلى شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له

DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r3.speaker: عطية
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r3.claim: The best way to handle an orphan’s property is to trade with it and seek profit for the orphan.
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r3.anchor: عن عطية في قوله {ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم إلا بالتي هي أحسن} قال: طلب التجارة فيه

DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r4.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r4.claim: The guardian should seek to make the orphan’s property grow.
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله {ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم إلا بالتي هي أحسن} قال: يبتغي لليتيم

DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r5.claim: A poor guardian may eat from the orphan’s property reasonably, but a wealthy guardian must abstain; the allowance cited in 4:6 concerns eating, not clothing.
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن زيد في قوله {ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم إلا بالتي هي أحسن

DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r6.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r6.claim: A guardian may not use the orphan’s money for his own cap or turban; his hand should remain with the orphan’s hand.
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r6.anchor: عن عكرمة {ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم} قال: ليس له أن يلبس من ماله قلنسوه

DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r7.speaker: الشعبي
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r7.claim: The orphan reaches full strength at puberty, when good and bad deeds begin to be recorded for him.
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r7.anchor: عن الشعبي في قوله {حتى يبلغ أشده} قال: الأشد الحلم إذا كتبت له الحسنات

DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r8.speaker: محمد بن قيس
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r8.claim: Full strength is reached at age fifteen.
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r8.anchor: عن محمد بن قيس في قوله {حتى يبلغ أشده} قال: خمس عشرة سنة

DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r9.speaker: ربيعة بن أبي عبد الرحمن
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r9.claim: Full strength means puberty, as indicated by the command to test orphans until they reach marriageable age in 4:6.
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r9.anchor:
عن ربيعة بن أبي عبد الرحمن
أنه كان يقول في هذه الآية: الأشد الحلم

DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r10.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r10.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم قال: الأشد: الحلم

DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r11.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r11.claim: Someone who carefully fulfills measures and weights with sincere intent will not be held to what exceeds his capacity.
DURR-FULL:v3p383#2/r11.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب قال: تلا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم {أوفوا المكيال والميزان بالقسط

DURR-FULL:v3p384/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p384/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v3p384/r1.claim: ‘With fairness’ means justice, and ‘We do not burden a soul’ means beyond its capacity.
DURR-FULL:v3p384/r1.anchor:
عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله {وأوفوا الكيل والميزان بالقسط}
يعني بالعدل

DURR-FULL:v3p384/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p384/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v3p384/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {بالقسط} قال: بالعدل

DURR-FULL:v3p384/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p384/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p384/r3.claim: The Prophet warns merchants that weighing and measuring is a responsibility through which earlier peoples perished; the compiler says the report is weak.
DURR-FULL:v3p384/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يا معشر التجار إنكم قد وليتم أمرا

DURR-FULL:v3p384/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p384/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p384/r4.claim: The Prophet says that when a people short-measure or short-weigh, God afflicts them with famine.
DURR-FULL:v3p384/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما نقص قوم الميكال

DURR-FULL:v3p384/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p384/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v3p384/r5.claim: When speaking, people should tell the truth.
DURR-FULL:v3p384/r5.anchor: عن ابن زيد في قوله {وإذا قلتم فاعدلوا} قال: قولوا الحق

DURR-FULL:v3p384/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p384/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v3p384/r6.claim: Speak truthfully even when the person concerned is a relative.
DURR-FULL:v3p384/r6.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله {وإذا قلتم فاعدلوا ولو كان ذا قربى

TIRMIDHI:3070/r1.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3070/r1.speaker: عبد الله
TIRMIDHI:3070/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says that anyone wishing to see the page bearing Muḥammad's seal should recite the commandments from 6:151 through 6:153; al-Tirmidhī grades the report ḥasan gharīb.
TIRMIDHI:3070/r1.anchor: عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، قَالَ مَنْ سَرَّهُ أَنْ يَنْظُرَ إِلَى الصَّحِيفَةِ الَّتِي عَلَيْهَا خَاتَمُ مُحَمَّدٍ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَلْيَقْرَأْ هَذِهِ الآيَاتِ

NASHR:v2p265#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p265#2/r9.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف وحفص
NASHR:v2p265#2/r9.claim: When تذكرون is addressed to listeners and has the following yāʾ, these four readers lighten the dhāl; the rest double it.
NASHR:v2p265#2/r9.anchor: فقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف وحفص بتخفيف الذال حيث جاء، وقرأ الباقون بالتشديد

BAQILLANI:v1p151/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p151/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAQILLANI:v1p151/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet recalled seeing Quss ibn Sa'ida at Ukaz atop a red camel, preaching that people should gather, listen, understand, and speak truthfully, since all living things die.
BAQILLANI:v1p151/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال لما وفد وفد عبد القيس على رسول الله قال أيكم يعرف قس بن ساعدة

BAQILLANI:v1p151/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p151/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAQILLANI:v1p151/r2.claim: At the Prophet's request, the delegation recited Quss's verses: generations leave signs, death has no return, and all people ultimately go where the dead have gone.
BAQILLANI:v1p151/r2.anchor: ثم قال رسول الله أيكم يروي شعره فأنشدوه

BAQILLANI:v1p151/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p151/r3.speaker: هشام عن أبيه
BAQILLANI:v1p151/r3.claim: Hisham, reporting from his father, says an Iyad delegation told the Prophet of Quss's verses about the dead in their graves being summoned on a coming Day, some naked and some in worn clothing.
BAQILLANI:v1p151/r3.anchor: عن هشام عن أبيه أن وفدا من إياد قدموا على رسول الله فسألهم عن حال قس بن ساعدة

BURHAN:v2p295/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p295/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p295/r1.claim: The command means when you intend to speak, speak justly; Arabic can name the intended act by the act itself because action follows the agent’s will and power.
BURHAN:v2p295/r1.anchor: وقوله ﴿ وإذا قلتم فاعدلوا ﴾ أي اردتم القول

BURHAN:v2p295/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p295/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p295/r7.claim: Treating an action as its intention avoids an absurd literal reading that would require renewed ablution after sitting and then standing to pray, and supports praying with one ablution.
BURHAN:v2p295/r7.anchor: وانما حمل على ذلك دون الحمل على ظاهره للدلالة على جواز الصلاة بوضوء واحد والحمل على الظاهر يوجب أن من جلس يتوضأ ثم قام إلى الصلاة

BURHAN:v2p433/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p433/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p433/r1.claim: Because speech is itself an act, the command to be just in speech establishes justice in actions all the more, as the ban on saying even uff to parents bars worse treatment.
BURHAN:v2p433/r1.anchor: وقوله ﴿ وإذا قلتم فاعدلوا ﴾ مع ان الفعل كذلك وقصد به ليعلم وجوب العدل في الفعل

ITQAN:v3p6/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p6/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v3p6/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the final three verses of al-An'am are clear, beginning with قل تعالوا.
ITQAN:v3p6/r5.anchor: وأخرج الحاكم وغيره عن ابن عباس قال

ITQAN:v3p6/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p6/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v3p6/r6.claim: In another report, Ibn Abbas locates three clear verses at قل تعالوا and three more at وقضى ربك ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه.
ITQAN:v3p6/r6.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم من وجه آخر عن ابن عباس
